items.summary: Computational homogenization and coupled multiscale simulations of heterogeneous materials require repeated solution of mechanical fields on Representative Volume Elements, which becomes prohibitively expensive for high-resolution three-dimensional microstructures. Machine-learning surrogates can accelerate these computations, yet most existing approaches predict fields for fixed macroscopic loadings and provide limited guidance on how to scale network architectures for high-resolution 3D tensor-field prediction. This work presents a U-Net surrogate trained to predict the full 36-component strain localization tensor field in voxelized concrete mesostructures at resolutions up to $256^3$. Training localization tensors are generated with an FFT-based linear elastic solver, and an extensive hyperparameter optimization is performed to derive scaling rules and an accuracy-speed trade-off analysis. The results show that only network width and depth need to be scaled with problem complexity, while several conventional U-Net design choices, such as doubling channels after downsampling, are suboptimal for this problem. The final neural network achieves a Mean Absolute Error of 1.118% on both the validation and the held-out test sets, and an inference speedup of approximately 8.7x over the FFT-based solver on an Nvidia H100 GPU. Generalization experiments reveal transfer across aggregate volume fractions and highlight the importance of training on diverse morphologies. To safeguard reliability, a Maximum Mean Discrepancy metric computed on internal feature maps is proposed for detecting out-of-distribution microstructures without costly reference computations.

items.title: Where are the shortest-path nodes in spatial networks?
items.summary: To predict the spatial distribution of shortest-path nodes, we propose a Gaussian estimate of the shortest-path node probability $π_{uv}(w)$, the probability that a node $w$ lies on a shortest path between a source $u$ and a destination $v$. According to the Gaussian estimate, three variables affect the shortest-path node probability $π_{uv}(w)$ and combine into one variable, the standardized detour $X_{uvw}$. In our simulations of hard and soft random geometric graphs in Euclidean, hyperbolic and spherical space, the standardized detour $X_{uvw}$ alone approximately determines how fast the shortest-path node probability $π_{uv}(w)$ decreases as the node $w$ moves away from the geodesic between the source $u$ and the destination $v$. We find and explain that, when the hopcount variance $σ^2(H_{uv})$ is very small, the shortest-path nodes have a discrete spatial distribution, a quantized distribution of shortest-path nodes. We further extend the study to spatially inhomogeneous networks, for which we propose a method to find the shortest-path nodes.

items.title: Limits of Cell Sensing in Observer-Absorber Assemblies
items.summary: Absorption improves concentration sensing for an isolated cell by suppressing rebinding correlations. We study how that local advantage competes with collective depletion in assemblies of cells coupled through the shared diffusion field. We introduce an observer--absorber model for permeant ligands sensed and consumed intracellularly with finite volumetric uptake rate $κ$ that continuously interpolates between Berg--Purcell monitoring and perfect absorption. For a single spherical cell, monitoring correlations, uptake statistics and optimal joint estimator are obtained analytically, and we characterize the transition between using observer and absorber information for sensing. In this case, all sensing strategies improve monotonically with $κ$. For arbitrary cell assemblies, we show that the long-time sensing problem can be reduced to solving for just two steady-state quantities for each cell: the mean internal concentration $\Cbar$ and its local sensitivity $\Tbar=-\partial_κ\log\Cbar$. In multicellular systems, uptake shortens rebinding memory, but it also depletes the signal available to neighbors. We reveal geometry-dependent optima for absorption rates, with Pareto fronts arising from competing objectives, as well as pure observing, pure absorbing, and partially absorbing regimes.

items.title: Energetic costs of reaching the physical limits of sensing
items.summary: Cells sense chemical gradients by absorbing ligand molecules, a nonequilibrium process that necessarily produces entropy. But how many molecules must a cell absorb, and therefore energy dissipate, to approach the physical limits of sensing? We derive closed-form expressions relating gradient sensing uncertainty to the number of absorbed molecules, which we link to entropy production. Unlike concentration sensing, which depends only on the total count, gradient sensing must resolve the angular asymmetry of the absorbed flux, adding a bounded dipole-contrast factor set by how strongly the cell absorbs. In the strong-signal regime, cells approach peak chemotactic alignment while absorbing a small fraction of the diffusion-limited uptake, with the required number of uptake events set by the relative concentration change across the cell. Re-analysis of Dictyostelium chemotaxis places the cell at 0.25% of that limit with a minor metabolic load, suggesting that sensing is limited by counting noise rather than by energetic cost.

items.title: Self-organisation through layering of $β$-plane like turbulence in plasmas and geophysical fluids
items.summary: Staircase formation and layering is studied in simplified, potential vorticity conserving models of plasmas and geophysical fluids, by investigating turbulent self-organisation and nonlinear saturation with different mechanisms of free energy production -- forcing or linear instability -- and with standard or modified zonal flow responses. To this end, staircase formation in both the standard and modified Charney-Hasegawa-Mima equations with stochastic forcing, along with two different simple instability driven models -- one from a plasma and from a geophysical context -- are studied and compared. In these studies, it is observed that $β$-plane turbulence that does not distinguish between zonal and non-zonal perturbations (i.e., standard zonal response) gradually forms large-scale, elliptic zonal structures that merge progressively, regardless of whether it is driven by forcing (though it should be slow enough to allow wave couplings) or by the baroclinic instability, using for example a two-layer model. Conversely, the plasma system, with its modified zonal response, can rapidly form straight, stationary jets of well-defined size, again regardless of the way it is driven: by stochastic forcing or by the dissipative drift instability. Furthermore, the instability-driven plasma system exhibits a phase transition between a zonal flow dominated state and an eddy dominated state. In both states, saturation is possible without large-scale friction.

items.title: Exponential Control of Adiabatic Time Reflection by Complex-Time Singularities
items.summary: Nearly identical temporal switching profiles can produce very different reflections even when both have small local adiabatic measures. In a lossless dielectric, we obtain this difference by adding a weak feature that changes the complex-time singularities while preserving monotonicity, endpoints, and central slope. A perturbation bounded by $0.6\%$ of the total inverse-permittivity change raises the reflected mode amplitude from $8.02\times10^{-10}$ to $1.28\times10^{-3}$. The complex action and pole residue predict this amplitude to within $0.32\%$. Within this waveform family, deviation and monotonicity constraints select three design regimes. At fixed deviation bound, reoptimization keeps the central feature's time scale comparable to the inverse incident angular frequency. The optimal amplitude is then proportional to $1/T$ as the switching time $T$ tends to infinity. Stretching a fixed profile gives exponential suppression. Full-wave Maxwell simulations resolve the backward packet, and filtering calculations quantify its sensitivity to modulation bandwidth.

items.title: Physics-informed Bayesian optimization of high-order harmonic generation in gases
items.summary: Optimization of high-order harmonic generation in gases is essential for attosecond science. Improving conversion efficiency from the infrared driving laser to the extreme-ultraviolet high-order harmonic radiation requires balancing microscopic single-atom dipole responses with macroscopic phase matching. The resulting conversion-efficiency landscape exhibits complex structures, such as the hyperbolic ridge in the pressure-length space, which can be difficult to accurately reconstruct using conventional Bayesian optimization. Here, we introduce a physics-informed Bayesian optimization framework that incorporates known physical scaling relations through nonlinear transformations of the search space. We first demonstrate the approach in the two-dimensional pressure-length space, where a direct grid scan enables detailed validation of the reconstructed landscape, before extending it to four dimensions, where exhaustive scanning becomes computationally impractical. In four dimensions, incorporating the pulse-duration scaling and a square-root transformation of conversion efficiency further improves the accuracy of the reconstructed landscape, as validated against an independent reference dataset. We also employ a threshold-based acquisition strategy to identify extended high-efficiency operating regions rather than isolated optimal points. Together, these results demonstrate that incorporating physical knowledge into Bayesian optimization improves the exploration and reconstruction of multidimensional high-order harmonic generation landscapes, extending its capabilities beyond locating individual optima.

items.title: SGAA: Independent active alignment of optical subgroups with uncompensated aberrations
items.summary: Uncompensated subgroup aberrations complicate subgroup-level active alignment (AA), as local image-quality extrema do not directly indicate the target alignment state. We propose SGAA, an image-learning-based method for independent active alignment of optical subgroups. Multi-field point spread functions (PSFs) from a dedicated test configuration characterize misalignment, while golden-sample reference calibration and unified regression predict adjustments toward a common optical target across toleranced specimens. In simulations with tolerances, one step reduced the mean differential wavefront RMS from $0.0592λ$ to $0.0086λ$, an 85.4% reduction. In alignment experiments on 100 production subgroups, SGAA increased the mean full-lens weighted modulation transfer function (WMTF) at 30, 50, and 80 lp/mm by 0.073, 0.065, and 0.040, respectively, relative to industrial MTF-based scanning. The 8 MP acceptance yield increased by 29.2 percentage points, and mean alignment time decreased from 43 s to 3.1 s. SGAA thus translates independent subgroup reference-state restoration into gains in full-lens imaging, acceptance yield, and alignment speed.

items.title: Purely elastic centre-mode instability in channel and pipe flows of a simplified Phan-Thien-Tanner fluid
items.summary: Recent work identified spatially localised midplane stress structures as the building blocks of chaotic behaviour in pressure-driven parallel shear flows of viscoelastic fluids. Such coherent structures are thought to originate from a linear centre-mode instability of the laminar state. In the absence of inertia, however, the Oldroyd-B and FENE-P constitutive models predict that this instability is confined to ultra-dilute polymer solutions and very large Weissenberg numbers in channel flow, while no purely elastic instability has been reported in pipe flow. Here, we study numerically the linear stability of channel and pipe flows of a simplified Phan-Thien-Tanner (sPTT) fluid and find a purely elastic centre-mode instability in both geometries across a wide range of polymer concentrations and at much lower Weissenberg numbers. Since the sPTT and FENE-P models have identical steady rheology and laminar profiles, their contrasting predictions indicate that the existence of the centre-mode instability is governed by the transient rheological response of the fluid. Our results suggest that the purely elastic centre-mode instability should be observable under realistic flow conditions. They also offer a means of discriminating between constitutive models.

items.title: Particle-hole asymmetry and a fluctuating pair-density-wave state in a lightly doped Mott insulator on the square lattice
items.summary: Whether a lightly doped Mott insulator on the square lattice supports robust $d$-wave superconductivity remains a central question in strongly correlated physics and in the microscopic theory of cuprate superconductivity. Experiments and numerical studies reveal a pronounced particle-hole asymmetry, pointing to a delicate competition among $d$-wave superconductivity, pair-density wave (PDW), stripe, charge-density wave (CDW), and antiferromagnetic correlations. Here we combine large-scale DMRG and finite-size PEPS to study the square-lattice $t$-$J$ model at low doping, $δ\leq 0.1$, while tuning the next-nearest-neighbor hopping $t'$ from the electron-like ($t'>0$) to the hole-like ($t'<0$) regime. The electron-like side supports robust, nearly uniform $d$-wave pairing, whereas decreasing $t'$ induces a period-two plaquette modulation and ultimately produces, on the hole-like side, a charge-dominated state with a strongly suppressed static pairing amplitude. DMRG calculations on open strips and squares, together with PEPS calculations on open squares up to $16\times16$ sites, support this evolution. On squares with $C_4$-symmetric Hamiltonians, both methods find that the pair correlations of the hole-like state select the plaquette momenta $(π,0)$ and $(0,π)$ and decay within a few lattice spacings, while the dominant charge-density modulation forms a bidirectional checkerboard whose period extrapolates to about $4a_0$, close to that observed in lightly doped Bi-2201. These observations establish a fluctuating plaquette PDW in the lightly doped hole-like regime, in which local pairs carry finite momentum but lack phase coherence. Our results firmly establish particle-hole asymmetry as a central organizing principle for competing pairing tendencies in the lightly doped $t$-$J$ model.

items.title: A Kato-Type Criterion for Vanishing Viscosity and Magnetic Diffusivity Limits for Compressible Magnetohydrodynamics
items.summary: In this paper, we investigate the vanishing viscosity and magnetic diffusivity limits for the compressible magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) equations on a smooth bounded domain in $\mathbb{R}^3$. Under the assumptions of interior regularity and uniform local boundedness near the boundary, we establish a Kato-type criterion under which finite energy weak solutions to the dissipative MHD system converge to weak solutions to the ideal MHD system as the viscosity and magnetic resistivity coefficients decrease to zero. In particular, under such criterion, the anomalous energy dissipation in the vanishing viscosity and diffusivity limits for MHD is precluded.

items.title: Modelling velocity gradient invariants in turbulence with Lundgren spiral vortex ensemble
items.summary: We investigate the joint probability density function $P(Q,R)$ of invariants $Q$ and $R$ of the velocity gradient tensor in the synthetic turbulent field formed from the Lundgren spiral vortex ensemble, which is referred to as the woven Lundgren turbulence (WLT). The WLT inherently captures non-Gaussian vorticity correlations and multiscale interactions, which are essential for reproducing $P(Q,R)$ observed in homogeneous isotropic turbulence. By analyzing the contributions of stretching, winding and dissipation processes in WLT, we demonstrate that the $Q$-$R$ diagram can be divided into three distinct physical regions: a head region dominated by stretching, a body region dominated by spiral vortex arms, and a tail region dominated by dissipation. We systematically vary three key parameters in WLT, the background strain rate, the cutoff age of spiral vortices and the viscous decay factor, and monitor the evolution of $P(Q,R)$ in different topological regions. It is revealed that increasing the stretching rate broadens the head region, larger cutoff ages enhance the inclination of the body region, and reducing viscous factors extends the tail region, thereby mimicking the effects of strain self-amplification and vortex stretching across scales. Based on WLT statistics, we establish and validate an explicit model of $P(Q,R)$ consisting of the stretching, spiral and dissipation contributions. Thus, the WLT provides a physically interpretable framework for understanding the relation between local geometry and global statistics of turbulence.

items.title: Mapping the limits of equilibrium in sheared granular liquid crystals
items.summary: While elongated particles in viscous fluids follow Jeffery orbits, their dynamics in dense granular flows remain unresolved. We demonstrate that sheared, low friction granular rods do not follow these orbits, but instead reach a quasi-equilibrium state quantitatively described by classical liquid crystal theory, with collisions providing effective thermal noise. This quasi-equilibrium analogy breaks down at two limits: low aspect ratios, where the theory incorrectly predicts isotropy, and high inter-particle friction, which drives a transition from steric screening to frictional gearing. We map this far-from-equilibrium breakdown using a phenomenological effective Ericksen number, establishing the limits of thermal thermodynamic analogies in driven athermal matter.

items.title: Two atoms with strong light-induced dipolar interactions
items.summary: We study how two atoms scatter light when they are closer than an optical wavelength and observe multiple new phenomena due to the strong interactions between laser-induced electric dipole moments. We identify a narrow range of densities where a fraction of the scattered light is coherent and shows a collective enhancement factor of two compared to independent atoms. The dynamics of the two-atom wavefunction can be observed through momentum distributions which reveal resonant ejection and depletion. Due to the tight confinement, the total fluorescence intensity strongly depends on the scattering length, since it originates from a narrow resonant (Franck-Condon) region. Furthermore, we measure how the probe laser intensity modifies the scattering length, which establishes a new way to shift Feshbach resonances. Our work provides microscopic insight into what occurs during photoassociation and parity projection in optical tweezers.

items.title: Depletion Capture and Rayleigh--Onsager Dynamics in Receptor-Mediated Endocytosis
items.summary: Receptor-mediated endocytosis requires a particle to approach a membrane in a crowded extracellular environment, form ligand-receptor bonds, and wrap the membrane against bending, tension, and cytoskeletal viscoelastic resistance. We develop a two-stage theory. The capture stage uses the exact ideal hard-sphere Asakura--Oosawa sphere-plane excluded-volume geometry. The wrapping stage combines a spherical-cap coordinate, a quadratic single-mode free energy, a standard linear solid with one internal strain variable, and a two-variable Rayleigh--Onsager (RO) gradient flow. The creep compliance is mapped exactly onto a long-time spring in parallel with a Maxwell branch, preserving both the creep retardation and stress relaxation times. The free energy is strictly convex by its Hessian convexity, and the linear wrapping system has two real negative eigenvalues and an explicit double-exponential solution. Two independent arguments establish strict monotonicity for positive initial drive: the irreducible Metzler structure with its positive semigroup and the interlacing of Laplace poles with positive velocity residues. The first-passage equation has a unique finite root below the unconstrained long-time limit. Normal-cone conditions specify the projected dynamics on $0\le x\le2$, and the projected system retains the Lyapunov inequality of the unconstrained gradient flow. From the same free energy we derive long-time adhesion thresholds, the threshold-minimizing radius, the finite-size window, and the critical cell modulus. The $95\%$ spherical-area criterion is treated as an operational near-complete threshold, with $90\%$, $95\%$, and $99\%$ compared. The capture analysis includes the exact overlap volume, depletion force, Carnahan--Starling pressure rescaling, Stokes approach time, and Brenner wall-drag correction.

items.title: CURRENT: A Recurrent Neural Network for Concurrent Spatial and Temporal Super-Resolution of 4D Flow MRI
items.summary: Objective: To improve the spatial and temporal resolution of aortic 4D flow MRI through a unified deep learning framework for post-acquisition super-resolution (SR) of reconstructed velocity vector fields. Methods: We propose CURRENT, a recurrent neural network that performs spatial and temporal SR with a single network architecture. Supervised training was conducted using paired low- and high-resolution datasets generated by embedding computational fluid dynamics simulations of aortic flow into in vivo thoracic MRI backgrounds, followed by controlled spatial and temporal downsampling. CURRENT was evaluated for two-fold spatial and temporal SR against 4DFlowNet and for two-fold spatiotemporal SR against sequential spatial and temporal SR pipelines based on 4DFlowNet. Image-based and k-space-based quantitative metrics were considered and conventional interpolation were used as baselines. In addition, the impact of CURRENT's spatiotemporal SR on physics-informed relative pressure estimation was assessed. Finally, the ability of CURRENT to generalize from synthetic training data to in vivo acquisitions was investigated. Results: CURRENT achieved superior spatial SR performance and comparable temporal SR performance to dedicated 4DFlowNet models while providing a unified solution for both tasks. Simultaneous spatiotemporal SR using CURRENT yielded more accurate relative pressure estimates than either spatial or temporal SR alone and outperformed sequential 4DFlowNet-based spatial and temporal SR approaches. Furthermore, the proposed model demonstrated promising generalization to in vivo 4D flow MRI data despite being trained exclusively on synthetic datasets. Conclusion: CURRENT provides a unified framework for spatial and temporal SR of 4D flow MRI. The proposed approach has the potential to enhance physics-based analysis and broaden the applicability of accelerated 4D flow MRI.

items.title: On bifurcations and traction forces on an obstacle in incompressible flow
items.summary: A systematic numerical investigation of flow-regime transitions in the two-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes flow past a confined circular cylinder is presented. For a fixed benchmark geometry, we observe a clear empirical correspondence between qualitative changes in steady traction profiles, understood here as the pointwise force density given by the Cauchy stress tensor on the obstacle boundary, and bifurcations in the long-time behavior of the unsteady Navier-Stokes equations. The observed transitions include onset of time-periodic oscillations, the appearance of multiple steady solutions and loss of effective symmetry. The well-known planar Schäfer-Turek benchmark is considered for Reynolds numbers up to 500. Several numerical techniques are employed to compute steady solutions, boundary traction profiles, and linear stability spectra such as duality-based approach for traction evaluation, deflation methods for detecting multiple steady states, and both two- and three-dimensional linear stability analysis. The results suggest that steady boundary traction profiles can serve as a sensitive diagnostic indicator of critical Reynolds numbers at which qualitative changes in flow dynamics occur. This suggests a computationally inexpensive, complementary approach for detecting flow-regime transitions within this benchmark configuration.

items.title: CV-TF-QKD
items.summary: We introduce a continuous-variable version of twin-field quantum key distribution, using independent Gaussian-modulated coherent states and an untrusted single-photon relay. Full-record reconciliation and a binary phase-disclosure protocol achieve nearly equal asymptotic key rates against collective attacks. At fixed weak input-referred excess noise per arm, both rates per relay use scale as $\sqrtη$, where $η$ is the end-to-end transmissivity. For phase disclosure, we establish composable security against general coherent attacks using a bounded test of preparation intensities and sign-parity complementarity. For specified apparatus parameters, finite-key calculations incorporating detector inefficiency, dark counts, phase fluctuations, and reference overhead predict rates exceeding the pure-loss and matched thermal-loss repeaterless bounds. These results extend the twin-field advantage to Gaussian-modulated continuous-variable quantum cryptography.

items.title: Accelerating matrix-free fast diagonalization and preconditioned linear solvers for higher-order finite element discretized elliptic problems on distributed GPUs
items.summary: The time to solution of an iterative solver depends on the number of iterations and the cost per iteration. This paper develops algorithms that reduce both for elliptic problems discretized with high-order continuous finite elements on distributed GPUs, implemented in a unified matrix-free code supporting CUDA, HIP and SYCL. A distributed direct fast-diagonalization (FD) Poisson solver provides exact solutions on tensor-product meshes with direction-wise grading and coefficients varying along one coordinate direction. Its tensor data stay distributed, moved between slab layouts by collective transposes or kept in place by a Schur-complement approach. It is also an exact coarse solver. A two-level hybrid Schwarz preconditioner with FD cell solves (HS-FD) is extended to 2:1 hanging-node octrees with exact local cell inverses, while a \(p\)-multigrid preconditioner with Chebyshev--Jacobi smoothing (CJ-\(p\)MG) resolves hanging-node constraints at every level within fused kernels. Both approaches exploit FP32, where cell shapes and coefficients allow, within an FP64 conjugate-gradient iteration, adaptively select replicated or distributed coarse levels, support block solves for multiple right-hand sides and determine all parameters from the operator without case-specific tuning. Comparisons with Jacobi-preconditioned conjugate gradients (Jacobi PCG), MFEM, nekRS and deal.II span uniform, graded and octree meshes, layered coefficients, and four applications across NVIDIA, AMD and Intel GPUs. The direct solver is two to three orders of magnitude faster than Jacobi PCG on uniform meshes. HS-FD converges in 11 iterations for an octree generalized Poisson problem across 8 to 1024 MI250X graphics compute dies. The results guide solver selection by mesh structure and coefficients

items.title: Characterization of BNLs 20 and 30 micrometer thick LGADs for the Electron Ion Collider
items.summary: The 20 and 30 micrometer thick Low-Gain Avalanche Detectors (LGADs) produced at Brookhaven National Laboratory (BNL) were evaluated. Detailed electrical measurements indicate well-formed and stable gain layers with consistently low leakage currents. Transient Current Technique (TCT) was used to evaluate the gain. Fast-laser timing studies demonstrate time resolutions at the level of a few tens of picoseconds. To assess operational longevity under realistic conditions for Electron-Ion Collider sub-detector systems, devices were irradiated with 30 MeV and 60 MeV protons to fluences of 10^13 to 10^14 neq/cm^2, enabling a focused study of radiation-induced effects on gain stability and timing performance.

items.title: Thermodynamics of words
items.summary: We introduce the word thermalization hypothesis according to which in a literary work there are effective interactions between words that drive them to thermalization where their word frequency distribution is the same as for the phenomenon of Rayleigh-Jeans (RJ) thermalization and condensation. In this concept, the different words play a role of classical oscillators (particles) and their word frequencies, or related tokens, are analogous to certain filling factors over energy state levels. The thermalization process is characterized by the conservation of total system energy, or total number of words/tokens, and total probability norm, or total number of different words. We apply this approach to analyze 16 literary works, including Bible, complete works of Shakespeare, and data from American National Corpus. We show that for these cases the effective system energy is very low and thus there is the RJ condensation phenomenon with a big fraction of total probability concentrated at the lowest energy states corresponding to a big fraction of rare words appearing only once or twice in the whole text. Such a RJ condensation is observed for light propagation in multimode optical fibers and other physical systems. We relate the thermalization of words to the recently proposed wealth thermalization for households in world countries. The economy concepts of Lorenz and Pareto curves, and also Zipf curves, are applied to the word frequency distributions of the selected 16 cases and it is shown that the thermalization theory gives a strikingly good description of real data.

items.title: An Alignment Microscope for Imaging Rotational Wavepacket Dynamics
items.summary: We introduce a new method for encoding polarization-angle-dependent molecular alignment signals directly into the transverse spatial profile of a femtosecond laser beam. The approach employs a pump-probe setup in a common-path geometry. A radial-azimuthal polarization converter placed in the probe beam produces a doughnut-shaped beam whose local polarization varies continuously with azimuthal angle, thereby encoding the full range of linear polarization orientations from 0 to $2π$ within a single transverse beam profile. Consequently, the angular dependence of the molecular response can be recorded simultaneously rather than reconstructed through sequential measurements at different polarization angles. By varying only the pump-probe delay, this spatial encoding enables single-shot acquisition of the complete angular response at each delay and real-time visualization of the evolving molecular alignment pattern as the delay stage is scanned. This technique has enabled the experimental realization of an alignment microscope.

items.title: PINNverse meets Jordan--Wigner: learning the Hamiltonian of long spin chains
items.summary: Inverse physics-informed neural networks (PINNverse) learn the parameters of a quantum Hamiltonian from measured expectation values, but the network output grows as $4^N$ with the number of qubits $N$. We show that, for spin chains with nearest-neighbor exchange interactions, the Jordan-Wigner transformation removes this exponential cost: the dynamics closes on an $N\times N$ one-body density matrix, so the network needs only $N^2$ outputs and the data are local observables measured in five global settings. Parasitic $ZZ$ couplings (crosstalk) are included through a time-dependent Hartree--Fock closure. With synthetic data, the same network first solves the equation of motion and then recovers the Hamiltonian parameters of chains of up to $50$ qubits, with couplings learned to better than $0.1\%$. Errors in the local frequencies of long chains are removed by a direct least-squares fit started from the network estimate.

items.title: Passive ladder-network representation of the radiation impedance of a spherical cap on a rigid sphere
items.summary: A loudspeaker in a closed box is modeled as a rigid sphere with an axially moving cap. For an axisymmetric cone-velocity profile, its radiation impedance is written as a network. Each spherical-harmonic mode has an impedance rational in frequency, realized exactly as a finite passive ladder of masses and compliances terminated in a resistance. Ideal transformers set by Legendre coefficients couple these ladders; truncated modes reduce to a residual mass. Despite the different geometry, the impedance resembles that of a baffled piston but, at equal volume velocity, has half its low-frequency resistance and about three quarters of its radiation mass.

items.title: The Feynman Dyson argument extended to the inhomogeneous Maxwell equations
items.summary: The Feynman-Dyson argument gives the homogeneous Maxwell equations but does not identify the sources in the other two equations with the charge and current carried by matter. Taking the homogeneous equations as given, we derive Gauss's law and the Ampere-Maxwell law for the sources entering the Lorentz force and the power delivered to matter. We assume, in particular, that the field densities and fluxes are at most quadratic in the fields and covariant under proper rotations. We require the same expressions for the sources to satisfy local energy and momentum conservation for every field that obeys the homogeneous equations, and to be continuous in spacetime along every smooth such field. The charge and current densities are then unique up to the values of $\varepsilon_0$ and $μ_0$. We also discuss how these assumptions might be relaxed.

items.title: Millisecond optical coherence and strong collective coupling in an integrated telecom rare-earth photonic platform
items.summary: Long-range quantum network nodes require the combination of strong light-matter coupling, long coherence times and in-situ spectral control at telecom wavelengths. The coherence of erbium in integrated devices is held back by its hosts, which do not simultaneously provide the weakly magnetic nuclear-spin environment and the well-defined substitutional sites found in coherence-optimised bulk crystals. Here we bring such an optimised crystal onto a photonic chip, by bonding an Er${^{3+}}$:CaWO${_{4}}$ host without an adhesive interlayer to a high-${Q}$ electro-optically tuneable thin-film lithium niobate microring resonator. At an effective temperature of 75mK and a field of only 0.2T, ions probed through a waveguide show an effective homogeneous linewidth of ${289\pm5}$Hz (${T_{\text{M}}=1.10\pm0.02}$ms), with spectral diffusion proceeding at ${86\pm18}$Hz and saturating at ${1.5\pm0.2}$kHz. Electro-optically tuning the resonator through the erbium optical transition resolves an avoided crossing with a collective cooperativity of ${C=6.7\pm0.4}$ at zero field and ${C=4.9\pm0.2}$ at 0.4T, where ${T_{\text{M}}}$ exceeds 1ms. Exploiting superhyperfine coupling to the host's ${^{183}}$W nuclear spins, we store and retrieve optical phase information over 5s with a visibility of ${0.935\pm0.015}$. Strong collective coupling, millisecond coherence and in-situ spectral tuning in a single device thus establish heterogeneous integration leveraging coherence-optimised hosts as a route to scalable telecom quantum networks.

items.title: Beyond Fourier and Laplace: The Hankel Neural Operator for Learning Solution Operators of Differential Equations
items.summary: Fourier and Laplace neural operators (FNO, LNO) learn kernel integral operators in a transform domain evaluated on a periodic grid. FNO has no explicit mechanism for boundaries, initial states or transients; LNO adds pole--residue symbols but evaluates them on the discrete Fourier grid with unconstrained poles. FNO's error is large on undamped oscillators and grows under grid refinement. We introduce the Hankel neural operator (HNO), derived from the structure of the solution operator. We prove that the solution operator of a well-posed linear constant-coefficient boundary-value problem on an interval is a Toeplitz operator with a rational kernel plus a finite-rank Hankel-type operator carrying boundary information. Classical results of Kronecker, Nehari and Adamyan--Arov--Krein characterise this kernel class: stable poles, finite Hankel rank and norm bounds independent of the interval length. HNO realises the class in three ways: a non-periodic convolution evaluated by the FFT, with a causal form; a closed-loop Lur'e operator for dynamics without fading memory; and a rational Fourier multiplier that contains FNO as a special case. Trained from data alone, HNO has the lowest mean test error on all nine LNO benchmarks and on the Burgers, Darcy and Navier--Stokes benchmarks of FNO; two of these differences, and the Navier--Stokes comparison with a parameter-matched FNO, are not statistically significant. On the six ODE problems it lowers the better baseline's mean error 2.1--5.2 times, and its Darcy error stays nearly constant from $85^2$ to $421^2$ grids, where FNO's grows eightfold. Ablations support each component. Code and data: \hnorepo{}.

items.title: Modeling runaway electron mitigation via passively driven plasma instabilities in a high-current tokamak
items.summary: A critical challenge for tokamak-based fusion power plants is the formation of high-current, relativistic runaway electron (RE) beams during abrupt confinement loss events called disruptions. RE beams may significantly damage machine components if left unmitigated, jeopardizing the operational and economic viability of fusion power plants. We present the first self-consistent extended magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) computational study of RE mitigation with a passively driven RE mitigation coil (REMC) in a high-current tokamak. RE generation and transport are coupled with REMC-driven MHD activity in a 3D simulation that models the thermal and current quench phases of a mid-plane disruption, together with the vertical displacement and final termination of the plasma and RE beam on SPARC -- a high-field, high-current tokamak designed to achieve a fusion gain Q > 1. We demonstrate that REMC-driven magnetic stochasticity can reduce the RE current by over an order-of-magnitude when compared to unmitigated disruptions. The final termination is mediated via a post-thermal-quench "cold" vertical displacement of the plasma, which, together with magnetic stochasticity, increases RE losses via scrape-off once the plasma contacts the first wall. These results demonstrate a viable mechanism for RE mitigation using passively driven plasma instabilities on high-current tokamaks.

items.title: Rheology of Parametric Odd Materials
items.summary: The design and control of rheological properties in active systems are crucial for developing functional materials with novel properties. While significant attention has been devoted to odd viscosity and odd elasticity, comprehensive odd rheological models remain scarce. Here, we introduce and characterise a platform-agnostic odd viscoelastic material, where complex responses arise from parametric control of internal rotational degrees of freedom and are triggered by coupling between normal and shear stresses. Such control can be achieved through either parametric driving or a parametric nonlinear feedback. We further show that this coupling can induce rotation-driven fluidisation, transitioning the material from an elasticity-dominated to a viscosity-dominated regime. Lastly, we show that the interplay between odd and even sectors enhances the nonlinear material response under large-amplitude oscillatory shear (LAOS). The findings outline a route to Floquet-engineered metafluids with programmable, non-reciprocal rheology.

items.title: Single-molecule strong optomechanical regimes in SERS via hybrid plasmonic cavities
items.summary: We identify enhanced strong coherent Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering (SERS) interactions facilitated by hybridized metallo-dielectric cavities with a resonant fluorescent molecule. By illuminating a detuned electronic transition near saturation via a narrowband hybrid plasmonic mode, we observe enhanced splittings in the Stokes and anti-Stokes spectra, revealing strong optomechanical coupling and nonlinear vibrational modifications at intensities far below irreversible SERS damage thresholds. We compute the second-order photon correlations that allows identifying the nonclassical character associated to these strong optomechanical interactions and SERS configurations that enables them to optically characterize the anharmonic character of the vibrational modes.

items.title: Data-driven regional traffic simulation from heterogeneous mobility sources
items.summary: Regional traffic simulators increasingly combine mobile-phone, road-sensor and GPS data, but what each source contributes is rarely clear. We present an agent-based simulator of daily traffic in Emilia-Romagna, Italy: phone data give trips and their timing, half of the road sensors set the traffic level, all sensors correct it locally, and GPS traces guide route choice. We measure what each source adds against predictors without simulation, on sensors kept out of parameter calibration in winter 2020 and partly shared with it in summer 2021; as these sensors informed some modelling choices, the evaluation is not fully independent. Total traffic is within 1% of observations in winter and 10% in summer, and the simulator ranks roads better than a road-type predictor (Spearman 0.67-0.68 against 0.41-0.48, winter). GPS improves this ranking, sensors improve local estimates, and timing comes mostly from the demand. Single-road errors remain similar to those of simple predictors, and the test of specific origin-destination pairings was underpowered and inconclusive. These findings provide a practical framework for assessing the contribution and limitations of heterogeneous data sources in regional traffic simulation.

items.title: Phase transitions and sharp localisation in anomalous localised resonance
items.summary: We study how detuning and absorption determine the strength and spatial extent of anomalous localised resonance in a two-dimensional quasistatic coated structure with shell permittivity $-1+c\ell^p+i\ell$, where $\ell>0$ is the loss and $c\ne0$, $p>0$ are fixed. Detuning can carry the material path through narrow resonances, producing intermittent rather than sustained power growth. For an explicit family of noncircular shells and a smooth exterior dipole source, both fixed, we classify the dissipated power under a quantitative smallness condition on the deformation. Depending on the detuning exponent and conformal source distance, the power diverges along the entire path, exhibits divergent peaks with vanishing gaps, or decays, including the threshold cases. We also identify the sharp conformal boundary beyond which the field, normalized by the square root of the dissipated power, converges locally to zero along every divergent-power sequence. For resonant sources, tangential reference crossings yield an explicit nonzero limit for the exterior gradient energy divided by the dissipated power at the critical radius.

items.title: Crowding and confinement of mesoscale swimmers in living droplets
items.summary: Droplets encapsulating active or living matter provide controllable platforms for studying collective dynamics and active interfacial actuation. However, prior work has largely focused on quasi-2D confinement, microscopic swimmers, or externally driven, non-living droplets. Here, we introduce living droplets internally activated by tens of enclosed mesoscale swimmers to study crowding and confinement in 3D with swimmer sizes comparable to the droplet radius. In large droplets with few swimmers, the droplet oscillation frequencies collapse onto the classical sessile-drop frequency-volume scaling. By increasing the number of swimmers or decreasing the droplet size, crowding and confinement alter the droplet oscillation frequencies and amplitudes as many-body or swimmer-droplet interactions start dominating. We develop a scaling-law framework linking the oscillation amplitude to swimmer speed through collision probability and momentum transfer, enabling indirect 3D velocimetry in the opaque, crowded droplets. Complementary quasi-2D experiments with direct tracking reveal dimensionality-dependent crowding effects, which we successfully describe with a kinetic theory-based model. We show distinct crossovers and strong-crowding asymptotic scalings of the swimmer speed with the dimensionless swimmer density, $U_{\mathrm{crowd}}\sim(N^{\ast})^{-1}$ in 3D and $U_{\mathrm{crowd}}\sim(N^{\ast})^{-1/2}$ in quasi-2D. Our results connect mesoswimmer encounter dynamics to macroscopic droplet mechanics and inform the design of bio-inspired micromachines, fluidic control, and sensing technologies.

items.title: QuantumBilliards.jl: An extensible, user friendly, high-performance Julia library for the large scale computation of spectra and eigenstates of quantum billiards and related problems
items.summary: We present QuantumBilliards.jl, an open-source Julia library providing a suite of numerical solvers for the two-dimensional interior Helmholtz eigenproblem with Dirichlet boundary conditions, a paradigmatic model in quantum chaos. The library implements conventional wavenumber-sweep techniques together with several accelerated eigensolvers: the Vergini--Saraceno scaling method, the expanded boundary integral method (EBIM), Beyn's contour-integral method, and the Compact Rational Krylov (CORK) method. It provides a common framework for constructing billiard geometries, exploiting discrete symmetries, computing eigenvalues and eigenstates, and treating smooth, cornered, and multiply connected domains. The library further includes reconstruction of eigenfunctions from boundary normal derivatives and the computation of Poincaré--Husimi (PH) phase-space representations. Available at: https://github.com/Quantum-Chaos-Julia/QuantumBilliards.jl.

items.title: Invariant universal averages and Bertrand's paradox: a response to Shackel
items.summary: In 2014, with D. Aerts we proposed a solution to the hard problem of Bertrand's paradox by means of a universal average over different ways of randomizing an entity. In his recent monograph, N. Shackel raises objections concerning the approximation by cellular densities, the restrictions used in their construction, the apparently trivial limit of their averages, the choice of a second-order probability law, and the dependence of the result on the naming of chords. We revisit these objections using the invariance-based formulation of the universal average. The first objection is well taken, and the approximation argument is repaired: an explicit sequence of bivalent cellular densities provides weak approximation of any prescribed probability measure, with an error bound for intervals. We show that any second-order selection law invariant under rearrangements of equal-length cells has the same uniform barycenter, independently of the particular densities and weights employed. For cellular densities, this conclusion holds exactly at every finite resolution. Thus, non-uniqueness of the second-order law does not prevent uniqueness of the average it produces, which is what entitles one to speak of 'the' universal average at all. Finally, we prove that no probability measure can be invariant under both these rearrangements and arbitrary changes of interval lengths. The reference geometry therefore cannot be obtained by averaging alone: it must be supplied by the physical modelization of the randomized entity. These results clarify the scope, and the limitations, of our original distinction between the easy and hard problems of Bertrand's paradox.

items.title: M-SHIVA 1.0: A Relativistic Resistive MHD Code for Heavy-Ion Collisions, with Applications to Momentum Anisotropy and Joule Heating in QGP
items.summary: We present M-SHIVA 1.0 (Magneto-resistive Solver for Heavy Ions with finite-Volume Algorithms), a (2+1)-dimensional relativistic resistive magnetohydrodynamics code for heavy-ion collisions in Cartesian and boost-invariant Milne coordinates. The present implementation treats inviscid dynamics and employs an implicit-explicit (IMEX) Runge-Kutta scheme for the stiff conductivity-dependent terms, together with complementary primitive-variable recovery procedures and generalized Lagrange multiplier (GLM) divergence cleaning. The code reproduces standard shock-tube, cylindrical-blast-wave and relativistic-rotor benchmarks. We use the framework to investigate the momentum anisotropy and electromagnetic energy transfer in an expanding quark-gluon plasma (QGP). In a controlled elliptic-fireball setup, the electromagnetic field modifies the total momentum anisotropy mainly through its direct contribution to the transverse stress tensor, while the matter anisotropy is only weakly affected. We further separate the electromagnetic work into mechanical Lorentz-force work and irreversible Joule heating. Applications to Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 62.4$ and $200$ GeV and Pb+Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 2.76$ TeV employ optical-Glauber matter profiles, spectator-generated electromagnetic fields, and a temperature-dependent electrical conductivity motivated by lattice-QCD results. The ratio of Joule heating to expansion cooling is approximately $10^{-14}$-$10^{-11}$ for Pb+Pb collisions at $2.76$ TeV, $10^{-8}$-$10^{-5}$ for Au+Au collisions at $200$ GeV and $10^{-7}$-$10^{-4}$ at $62.4$ GeV, with no appreciable conductivity dependence of the matter or total momentum anisotropy. Resistive heating thus grows by orders of magnitude with decreasing collision energy but remains negligible compared with longitudinal expansion cooling for all systems considered.

items.title: Off-focus detection for SNR enhancement in coherent single-pixel imaging
items.summary: Coherent single-pixel imaging (CSPI) enables amplitude- and phase-resolved computational imaging with a single coherent detector, offering particular advantages in spectral regimes where high-performance detector arrays remain unavailable. In conventional Fourier-plane CSPI, the detector is typically placed at the focal point to maximize the collected power. However, this focal position does not necessarily maximize the reconstruction fidelity for image reconstruction in the presence of system nonidealities. Here, we introduce detector position as an additional degree of freedom for CSPI optimization. We show that appropriately selected off-focus Fourier-plane positions can improve reconstruction performance by suppressing fluctuation-sensitive coherent backgrounds while preserving spatially encoded signals. Experimentally, using a programmable liquid-crystal terahertz spatial light modulator and coherent heterodyne detection, we demonstrate improved amplitude and phase reconstruction from selected off-focus channels compared with focal detection. A symmetric off-focus pair with complementary transverse-wave-vector weighting further enhances image fidelity, contrast, and compressive-sampling robustness through coherent channel fusion. These results establish detector-position engineering as a new strategy for enhancing the robustness and information efficiency of CSPI.

items.title: Bubbles in highly porous media: Clogging and unclogging at constrictions
items.summary: Gas bubble transport through highly porous transport layers (PTLs) is a key process in electrochemical devices such as proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers, where bubbles generated at catalyst surfaces must migrate through complex porous networks. To understand this process, we focus on model systems, namely the motion of single, paired and multiple bubbles in capillaries and study these by combining analytical modeling, three-dimensional color-gradient lattice Boltzmann simulations, and X-ray radiography. For single bubbles, we derive an analytical expression for the critical Bond number separating passage from clogging and show that, in the low deformation regime, it accurately predicts this transition in circular capillaries. Extending the study to bubble pairs, we uncover additional clogging and unclogging pathways, including hydrodynamic unclogging driven by pressure buildup in the interbubble film, and coalescence-induced clogging and unclogging. By mapping our results as functions of confinement ratio and Bond number, we define distinct dynamical regimes that control bubble passage. Experiments on bubble chains rising through highly porous nickel foams confirm the predicted clogging and unclogging mechanisms.

items.title: SiPM optical readout of a PICOSEC Micromegas precise timing detector
items.summary: By combining a Cherenkov radiator with a semi-transparent photocathode and a two-stage Micromegas amplification element, PICOSEC Micromegas detectors have achieved <20 ps charged-particle time resolution with electronic readout of induced signals. Building upon this performance, we describe SiPM-based optical readout as a novel technique for PICOSEC Micromegas detectors. Single-channel detector prototypes based on glass Micromegas technology were read out with an array of SiPMs. To allow operation in a strongly quenched gas mixture, a solid wavelength shifter is integrated in the glass Micromegas to convert UV scintillation to the visible range and maximise scintillation light output. Timing performance of glass Micromegas in electronic and optical readout modes is compared and <150 ps time resolution is achieved by optically read out scintillation light signals. The achievable spatial resolution from centre-of-gravity reconstruction of event positions from the amplitudes of signals on multiple SiPM channels is σ = 1.25 mm. This demonstrates the possibility of dual-readout of PICOSEC glass Micromegas: electronic signals and optical signals. Finally, camera-based optical readout is presented to demonstrate imaging as another avenue for position reconstruction.

items.title: Design and Operation of a 3-Crystal Multi-Volume Reflection Array for Loss Reduction in CERN SPS Slow Extraction
items.summary: The flux of protons slow-extracted from the CERN Super Proton Synchrotron (SPS) to the North Area experiments is limited by the induced radioactivity of the beam lost on the electrostatic septum during third-integer resonant extraction. Crystal shadowing, in which a thin bent silicon crystal deflects the protons that would otherwise hit the septum wires, has been in operation at the SPS since 2021; a single crystal at a non-local position halved the extraction losses relative to the local crystal alone, short of the fourfold reduction that future high-intensity operation requires. In this paper, the design, deployment and operation of a 3-crystal Multi-Volume Reflection Array (MVRA) at the non-local position in the fourth long straight section (LSS4) are presented. The array geometry was designed by Multi-Fidelity Bayesian Optimization (MFBO), combining a multilayer-perceptron surrogate with full particle tracking; it predicts a fourfold loss reduction with three crystals and up to tenfold with an ideally aligned array of four to five. At its optimum the as-built array reaches, and at its best point exceeds, the predicted factor of four, and beam dynamics simulations matched to the measured position and angle scans reproduce their shape to within 0.04 of the crystals-retracted loss. In physics production an extremum-seeking controller has held the array on its operating plateau, with a median loss reduction by a factor of 3.6 over 1.14 x 10^5 extraction cycles relative to the pre-shadowing baseline. The remaining margin to the target, the limitations of the present installation and the upgrade to a 4- or 5-crystal array are discussed.

items.title: Additively manufactured ceramic platforms for miniaturized optical frequency references and robust atomic sensor systems
items.summary: Transferring atomic quantum sensors from laboratory-scale physics packages to compact, alignment-free sensor heads suitable for field and space deployment requires a structural platform that combines mechanical, thermal, and optical functionality within a single, manufacturable component. We present such a platform based on additively manufactured technical ceramics: lithography-based ceramic manufacturing is used to fabricate monolithic micro-optical benches with application-specific mounting geometries, while high-precision active alignment and adhesive bonding realize long-term stable optical assemblies through micro-integration. As a first system-level demonstrator, we present a micro-integrated optical frequency reference based on Doppler-free spectroscopy of the rubidium D2 line, integrated within a 6 mL Al2O3 module. A laser stabilized to the reference reaches a fractional frequency instability of $3\times10^{-12}$ at 1 s. We extend the platform to a compact optically pumped magnetometer, exploiting the magnetic cleanliness and tailored thermal properties of high-purity ceramics for a 7 mL sensor head with picotesla sensitivity aimed at space-borne biomagnetometry, and to a micro-integrated optical dipole trap with active MEMS-mirror beam steering for cold-atom manipulation. Together, these demonstrators show that ceramic additive manufacturing and optical micro-integration form a versatile, robust platform for compact atomic sensor systems in field and space applications.

items.title: From OpenSPIM to FlowSPIM: Enhancing the versatility of a light-sheet microscope through an iterative design process
items.summary: Light-sheet microscopy is ideal for the 3D imaging of large biological specimens, yet systematic documentation on adapting microscope designs to diverse experimental requirements remains limited. We present the iterative process used to design and build a modular light-sheet microscope and adapt it to different sample types and experimental conditions, including live and fixed zebrafish, Drosophila, and mouse gastruloids, as well as cellulose nanocrystals. Starting from a stripped-down OpenSPIM platform, we gradually made our microscope more versatile by adding hardware such as additional laser channels and optical filters, and new protocols for sample handling. In its final iteration, FlowSPIM is a new flow-based incubation technique for 3D tissue culture.

items.title: Analytic Solution to Cumulative Coulomb Scattering in Boltzmann Theory
items.summary: In plasmas, frequent soft Coulomb collisions gradually transfer energy and momentum, whereas a single close collision can change both abruptly and redirect a particle. This coexistence can shape runaway-electron avalanches in tokamaks and alpha-particle heating in inertial fusion, yet no first-principles analytic theory has determined how the cumulative statistics evolve under plasma conditions. Fokker--Planck and moment-matched models reproduce average transport but do not determine how scattering evolves from isolated events to cumulative relaxation across plasma conditions. Here we resolve this long-standing problem directly from Boltzmann theory. By asymptotically rescaling the exact angular expansion, we obtain the first quantitative map of the single-collision, core-tail coexistence, and low-order relaxation regimes within a unified Boltzmann framework. The rescaling also provides explicit analytic representations of the angular distribution across these regimes without empirical transition parameters. The theory further shows that small-angle models differ from the Boltzmann distribution even in the forward core, so appending a large-angle tail to a conventional core cannot recover the collision statistics. In fast-electron transport, this full-range redistribution leaves mean energy loss nearly unchanged yet counterintuitively enhances beam concentration and modifies the energy flux delivered to a finite region.

items.title: Efficient photo-ionizing elimination of detrimental electric fields for Rydberg atoms
items.summary: Rydberg atoms are highly sensitive to external electric fields due to their exaggerated electronic properties. This unique feature underpins many of their applications in quantum science. However, uncontrolled stray electric fields can be detrimental, severely degrading quantum control. In this work, we demonstrate a novel scheme that efficiently creates an in-vacuum charge source by photo-ionizing laser-cooled atoms and eliminates detrimental electric fields in a Rydberg-atom tweezer array platform, using only readily available resources. With this method, we began with Stark-ionized Rydberg continuum spectra caused by a large, unknown stray electric field of more than $10~\mathrm{V/cm}$ and ultimately recovered well-resolved coherent excitation of individual Rydberg states after eliminating the residual field to an upper limit of $20(1)~\mathrm{mV/cm}$. Our method applies directly to existing Rydberg-atom platforms and other experiments sensitive to stray electric fields.

items.title: Time-Varying Photonics: A Review of Theory, Phenomena, and Experimental Platforms
items.summary: Time-varying photonics opens new avenues for controlling waves through engineering material properties in time. In this review, we introduce the basic concepts and theoretical tools for describing temporal interfaces, time-periodic systems, and space-time media, as well as review representative experimental approaches across different photonic and wave platforms. We further discuss characteristic phenomena enabled by temporal modulation, including coherent wave control, parametric amplification, nonreciprocity, and topological effects. This review provides a unified pathway for understanding time-varying photonics and outlines its current challenges and future opportunities in both fundamental physics and practical applications.

items.title: A Hardware-Trained Generative Quantum Eigensolver for Sample-Based Quantum Diagonalization of Organotin Hydroxides up to 70 Qubits
items.summary: Quantum hardware can provide feedback for training circuit generators beyond the reach of exact classical simulation. We train generative quantum eigensolver (GQE) policies, transformers conditioned on molecular descriptors, to generate the state-preparation circuits for sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD). Training runs first on a noiseless simulator and then with the IBM Heron processor ibm_kobe inside the loop, at 46 and 70 qubits ($1.2 \times 10^8$ shots for the four main training runs). A classical CCSD(T) reference energy of the training molecules enters only an admission gate and two auxiliary reward terms. During hardware training, a reward penalty prevents collapse to circuits that sample only the Hartree-Fock determinant. Policies trained on transition-metal complexes are applied without retraining to Sn(OH)$_3$-Me and its hydrates, minimal models of organotin photoresists for extreme-ultraviolet lithography, from 32 to 70 qubits. After one round of hardware sampling, followed by classical ranking and recovery of the cached counts with the molecular Hamiltonian and no further QPU calls, 27 of 28 runs at 46-70 qubits are within 15 mHa of the density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) reference (median 4.5 mHa), and in all eight runs with an untrained control the trained policy is more accurate. At 56-70 qubits the selected circuits use 34-72 times fewer two-qubit gates than the local unitary cluster Jastrow (LUCJ) circuit transpiled for the same device. These results demonstrate that circuit generators can be trained with quantum hardware at 70 qubits.

items.title: Hierarchical interfacial anchoring for durable perovskite solar cells
items.summary: Although inverted perovskite solar cells now deliver certified efficiencies approaching their single-junction limits, their practical deployment remains constrained by the thermo-mechanical fragility of buried interfaces under realistic temperature fluctuations. Here, we identify thermo-mechanically driven, stress-accumulation-dominated adhesion failure at self-assembled monolayer-based buried interfaces as a critical failure mode in inverted perovskite solar cells. To address this issue, we propose an interfacial robustness design strategy based on a homometallic halide pretreatment, which constructs a chemically compatible and highly anchorable interfacial environment on transparent conductive oxides to guide the ordered assembly of SAMs. This interfacial treatment increases the density of surface hydroxyl species and enables hierarchical multipoint interfacial anchoring dominated by metal-oxygen coordination, with Cl- induced hydrogen-bonding interactions acting cooperatively, thereby enhancing anchoring robustness and improving tolerance to thermo-mechanical stress accumulation. With this interfacial strategy, the devices achieve a power conversion efficiency of 27.3% (26.9% certified) and retain 94% of their initial efficiency after 400 temperature cycles between -40 and 85 degrees C (ISOS-T-3). These results demonstrate that rational regulation of buried interfacial anchoring architectures can simultaneously enhance device efficiency and long-term operational reliability, offering a viable pathway toward high-efficiency and durable perovskite photovoltaics.

items.title: Improving the vibration isolation efficiency of chiral phononic crystals through viscoelastic damping
items.summary: Mechanical phononic crystals attenuate vibration transmission in a wide frequency range called the bandgap. Chiral phononic crystals have demonstrated their ability to achieve low-frequency bandgaps while maintaining a high static stiffness. However, their design is non-trivial because of the complex geometry involved. Furthermore, bandgap generation in phononic crystals relies on wave scattering rather than energy dissipation, which leads to important local vibration amplitudes. In this paper, viscoelastic inserts are introduced with two goals: improve the crystal's tunability in terms of stiffness and bandgap properties, and employ damping to reduce internal resonances. First, the fundamental effect of viscous damping in phononic crystals is investigated through analytical equivalent models, showing that moderate damping improves the vibration isolation by merging multiple bandgaps. As a real-world example, highly viscoelastic polyurethane is studied by examining the influence of its frequency-dependent storage modulus and loss factor. Three crystals with different viscoelastic inserts are manufactured and the measured force transmissibility is successfully compared to the numerical models. The results show that the storage modulus correlates strongly with vibration isolation efficiency, defining both the frequency range and the maximum force reduction, whereas a loss modulus broadens the vibration isolation frequency range without negatively affecting its efficiency when it stays below a critical threshold value.

items.title: Structural Perturbations and Full Field Evolution in Tapered Spun Ring-Core Fiber Amplifiers
items.summary: We theoretically investigate the complex full-vector modal field evolution in tapered spun ring-core fiber amplifiers subject to structural perturbations, utilizing a combined coupled-mode theory and rate-equation model. To provide a comprehensive characterization, we introduce a normalized complex modal-state fidelity factor that simultaneously incorporates intensity, phase and polarization into a single quantitative measure. We demonstrate that the twist pitch of the structure can be purposely tuned to either suppress or leverage the effect of specific geometrical perturbations. These findings provide insight into the physical conditions governing modal stability, establishing a robust mechanism for highly efficient in-fiber OAM mode conversion.

items.title: Linear stability of viscous stratified shear flows with arbitrary equations of state
items.summary: A mathematical framework is developed to analyse the linear stability of viscous stratified flows with arbitrary equations of state. The model accommodates equations of state of the form $p=Φ(T,ρ)$ or $ρ=φ(T)$, together with a set of governing dimensionless parameters. Density stratification is unrestricted, allowing for the study of non-Boussinesq effects. A low-Mach-number approximation is employed to filter out acoustic phenomena. The framework is applied to two viscous stratified configurations of plane Couette flow: a triple-layer density profile supporting the Taylor--Caulfield instability (TCI), and a differentially heated supercritical fluid exhibiting a distinct instability mechanism. Following validation against reference studies, we present new results showing that non-Boussinesq effects weaken the viscous TCI, whilst viscosity can further destabilise the supercritical fluid instability, in contrast to the stabilising influence of buoyancy.

items.title: An infrared divacancy color center in bulk hexagonal diamond for quantum communication
items.summary: Intrinsic color centers are investigated in bulk hexagonal diamond as potential emitters for fiber-based quantum communication. Hybrid density functional theory and constrained-occupation delta SCF calculations identify five carbon-vacancy and divacancy configurations with stable optical excited states. A comparison of their radiative and nonradiative properties within a three-point configuration-coordinate model identifies the positively charged axial divacancy, VVa1+, as the most promising candidate. It exhibits the highest calculated zero-phonon-line (ZPL) emission rate of 43.9 MHz and ZPL quantum efficiency of 11.8% among the five candidates. Its weak structural relaxation yields a Huang-Rhys factor of 0.395, while a multimode photoluminescence calculation gives a Debye-Waller factor of 69.37%, indicating a dominant zero-phonon contribution. The predicted ZPL at 0.603 eV (2057.3 nm) also has the smallest photon-energy separation from the 1310 and 1550 nm telecom targets among the candidates. These results identify VVa1+ as a promising intrinsic color center for fiber-based quantum communication, with quantum frequency upconversion offering a route from its strong infrared ZPL to the telecom O and C bands.

items.title: Reading Why: Born-Measured Attention with Exact Word Evidence on Light and Qubits
items.summary: When a language model answers, we can usually only estimate why. We build a transformer in which every nonlinearity is a quadratic detection (an interference, a balanced interferometric reading or a camera) and the output is a Born probability: attention $|\langle q|k\rangle|^2$, the form of the Born rule, normalised over each row, a measured product in place of the feed-forward nonlinearity, and a Born readout; between detections a classical controller squares, divides, rescales and re-encodes. With its denominators held at their values for the input, each class probability is a polynomial in the word amplitudes, so its integrated-gradient evidence is computed by a finite quadrature with no quadrature error: the words' contributions sum to the class probability above its no-information share, to $10^{-13}$ or better. On e-SNLI natural language inference the model reaches 77.45 +- 0.91 % test accuracy, level within the spread of three seeds with a softmax transformer of the same size (76.62 +- 0.36 %). Deleting the word its evidence ranks first changes the answer in 44 % of test pairs, out of the 53 % any single deletion can change, against 32 % for the softmax model's integrated gradients and 31 % for the Born Transformer's own attention. The same weights compile exactly to optoelectronic optics (simulated), and its attention overlaps to Hadamard tests on qubits; a separate coherent attention layer becomes one post-selected circuit (852 CNOTs on 23 qubits). On IBM's ibm_kingston, reading only the attention overlaps, the device gave the model's answers on the two shortest test pairs, also when the one word that decides one of them was deleted; with calibration circuits as deep as the overlaps, each word's evidence with the device's attention row sums followed the exact evidence on one pair (correlation 0.997) and on the other less closely (0.962).

items.title: Kinetic Non-Equilibrium Receptivity Analysis of Hypersonic Flows via a Complex Linearized Unified Gas-Kinetic Scheme
items.summary: In the near-space regime, local rarefaction near the leading-edge shock and wall degrades Navier-Stokes-based stability and receptivity analyses due to velocity slip, temperature jumps, and non-equilibrium transport. The unified gas-kinetic scheme (UGKS) provides a multiscale kinetic description spanning continuum to rarefied regimes. Building on this, a complex linearized UGKS (CLUGKS) is developed: first-order perturbations of the discrete UGKS residual are formulated under a time-harmonic assumption with complex amplitudes, converting disturbance equations into a steady elliptic system solved via pseudo-time marching with LU-SGS acceleration. Consequently, kinetic shock structures, wall slip, temperature jumps, and non-Fourier heat fluxes are inherently captured without hybrid coupling. Three benchmarks verify the framework: a standing acoustic wave at an isothermal wall, a Mach 2 normal shock interacting with an obliquely incident acoustic wave, and freestream acoustic receptivity of a hypersonic blunt wedge. The scheme is applied to argon blunt-wedge flows at equivalent altitudes of 40 km and 50 km. At 40 km, UGKS and Navier-Stokes wall responses agree well in period and phase, while wall slip sustains a weakly positive spatial growth rate in UGKS downstream. At 50 km, intensified rarefaction produces a kinetic temperature precursor and a thickened, merged shock layer; while wall-pressure responses remain close, significant deviations emerge in temperature and heat-flux disturbances. These findings show that while continuum models capture dominant wall-pressure signatures under moderate rarefaction, resolving kinetic non-equilibrium across the shock-particularly its thermal footprint-is essential at higher altitudes.

items.title: Kinetics of segregation of topologically-modified ring polymers in cylindrical confinement
items.summary: In Escherichia coli (E. coli), entropic repulsion between the two daughter DNA ring polymers under cylindrical confinement is believed to be an important factor governing chromosomal segregation. The repulsion can be enhanced by topological modifications, i.e., by the introduction of internal loops at certain locations along the contour of the circular DNA. However, the effect of topological modifications on the rate of segregation of ring polymers remains unclear. Therefore, we systematically varied the number and the contour length of loops introduced at selected locations by crosslinking monomers. The appropriate crosslinking was motivated by observations that extruded loops are located mainly near the origin of replication (ori-proximal) region of the E. coli chromosome. This resulted in the chains becoming intrinsically anisotropic. Using Langevin dynamics simulations of these topologically modified bead-spring polymers, we calculated the time required for segregation under cylinder confinement. With certain caveats, we found that increasing the number of loops resulted in a decrease in the time of segregation. In line with past work, we propose that this is due to the increase in the entropic repulsion between the polymers upon increasing the number of loops. In addition to the number of loops, the contour length of the loops and the mutual orientation of the (anisotropic) chains in the initial configurations played a role in determining the time of segregation.

items.title: Stress-controlled avoided-crossing evolution of an optical microresonator induced by inter-fibre side coupling
items.summary: Analogies between quantum mechanics and photonics provide a powerful means of transferring concepts and phenomena between the two fields. Photonic analogues offer a distinctive advantage by allowing us to engineer and continuously vary parameters fixed by the microscopic structure of quantum systems, revealing richer behaviour. Building on these analogies, the recent demonstration of widely tunable microresonators formed by side coupling between optical fibres marked a significant advance in the development of reconfigurable resonant photonic systems. However, those methods offered no direct way to reach the centre of the avoided crossing, where the uncoupled fibre cutoff frequencies coincide and the modes hybridise most strongly. Here, we introduce an additional tuning degree of freedom by axially stretching a straight fibre coupled to a bent fibre. At essentially fixed coupling geometry, this lets us sweep the detuning between their uncoupled cutoff frequencies through zero. As the avoided crossing is approached, the induced microresonator's resonance band widens. Beyond the crossing, the band narrows and, strikingly, appears to "hang" below the stretched fibre's rising cutoff frequency. Our experimental results agree with coupled-mode theory and indicate the feasibility of 100 MHz-scale control of the straight-fibre cutoff frequency and the resonator spectral height over a tuning range of about 100 GHz, using a relative elongation of order $10^{-3}$.

items.title: High-quality electron beam generation from laser wakefield accelerators for driving compact free electron lasers
items.summary: Despite the successful demonstration of compact free electron lasers (FELs) driven by laser wakefield accelerators (LWFAs), the pursuit of further enhancements in high-gain compact FELs presents a challenge due to the limitations in electron beam quality. In this work, we pinpoint the pivotal physics and optimization strategies for high-quality single-stage LWFAs that are crucial for high-gain FELs. We have delved into the synergistic injection mechanism, where the self-evolution injection threshold is far from reached at the injection position, with both the shock front and self-evolution of the laser playing a role in the injection process. A thorough discussion has been provided on the beam-quality degradation and optimization strategies, in terms of global (slice) energy spread and projected (slice) emittance. With the goal of achieving high-gain FELs driven by LWFAs, we have also explored the synthesis quality of the electron beam to determine an optimized power gain length. A comprehensive start-to-end simulation has been conducted, demonstrating the effectiveness of compact FELs powered by these high-quality electron beams. The resulting radiation reaches the saturation regime after a 4.5-meter-long undulator, with an energy of 17.4 μJ and a power of 6.0 GW at a wavelength of 23.9 nm. This proposed scheme offers not only a framework for optimizing beam quality in LWFAs, but also a promising path for future compact LWFA-driven FELs to achieve saturated regimes, opening up new possibilities for widespread applications.

items.title: Wide Field 3D Color Topography for Steep-slope Structures
items.summary: Three-dimensional (3D) topography measurement is essential for industrial inspection and scientific research. However, existing techniques are limited by an inherent trade-off between resolution, speed, color imaging capability and the ability to measure large-angle surfaces. To overcome these limitations, we propose a novel method that integrates ring light illumination based wide-field 3D imaging with an iterative shape-from-focus (SFF) algorithm.
