items.summary: We study the mixing behavior of three q-deformed card shuffles on $\mathcal{H}_q(S_n)$: the short systematic scan introduced in \cite{DiaconisRam2000}, the $q$--deformed random--to--random shuffle introduced in \cite{AxelrodFreedBraunerChiangComminsLang2024}, and the $q$--deformed $k$--star transposition shuffle, whose $q=1$ counterpart was studied in \cite{ArfaeeNestoridi}. The first two chains were diagonalized in \cite{DiaconisRam2000} and \cite{AxelrodFreedBraunerChiangComminsLang2024}, respectively. Here, we diagonalize the $q$--deformed $k$--star transposition shuffle and use the spectra of the three chains to study their mixing behavior. For fixed $q>1$, we prove that all three exhibit total variation and $\ell^2$ cutoff. For the short systematic scan, these improve both the upper and lower bounds of Diaconis and Ram \cite{DiaconisRam2000}.

items.title: GAIA: Geometry-Adaptive Operator Learning for Forward and Inverse Problems
items.summary: Operator learning for partial differential equations (PDEs) on arbitrary geometries builds fast neural surrogates for large-scale simulation. While recent geometry-adaptive neural operators have made substantial progress, they are mainly designed for forward problems in which inputs and outputs share the same spatial domain. This limits their applicability for boundary value problems (BVPs) and inverse problems, where inputs and outputs may live on different domains. We introduce the Geometry-Adaptive Integral Autoencoder (GAIA), an operator learning model that encodes the domain boundary and the interior field distribution into geometry tokens, and conditions integral transform layers on these tokens via cross-attention, allowing the kernel to adapt locally to geometric features. This yields an architecture capable of learning solution operators for forward and inverse problems on arbitrary domains, solving each in a single pass at inference without per-domain optimization, iterative refinement, or graph construction. We evaluate GAIA on seven 2D and 3D benchmarks, four of which are new or substantially extended benchmarks for inverse problems and BVP: electrical impedance tomography, optical tomography, 3D Darcy flow on varying geometries, and a modified setting of the Poisson BVP on mechanical components benchmark (MCB). GAIA sets new state-of-the-art results on every inverse and BVP task, reducing median relative $L^2$ error by 64% on airfoil flow reconstruction and 22% on EIT relative to the next best amortized method, and outperforming all baselines on every shape category of MCB. On other forward problems, GAIA is competitive with specialized solvers while maintaining stable accuracy across point resolutions on which transformer-based baselines degrade.

items.title: The strong fractional choice number can exceed the choice number by an arbitrarily large amount
items.summary: Erdős, Rubin and Taylor asked whether $(a,b)$-choosability implies $(am,bm)$-choosability for all positive integers $a,b,m$. Dvořák, Hu and Sereni disproved this for $(a,b,m)=(4,1,2)$ and asked whether a $3$-choosable graph can fail to be $(6,2)$-choosable. Following an earlier discussion by Jiang and Zhu, Li and Zhu asked whether every $k$-choosable graph is $(kb+1,b)$-choosable. Equivalently, Xu and Zhu asked whether $\mathrm{ch}_f^s(G)\le\mathrm{ch}(G)$ for every graph $G$, where $\mathrm{ch}(G)$ is its choice number and $\mathrm{ch}_f^s(G)$ is its strong fractional choice number, defined as the infimum of the real numbers $r$ such that $G$ is $(a,b)$-choosable for all positive integers $a,b$ with $a/b\ge r$. In this paper, we prove that, for all integers $t\ge0$ and $b\ge7t+2$, there is a planar graph of choice number three that is not $(3b+t,b)$-choosable. This answers the question of Dvořák, Hu and Sereni affirmatively and the other questions negatively, even for planar graphs. Next, for all integers $k\ge4$, $t\ge0$ and $b\ge3t+2$, we construct a graph of choice number $k$ that is not $(kb+t,b)$-choosable, using only the six-vertex wheel $W_5$ as its core gadget. The case $t=0$ and $b=2$ recovers the result of Dvořák, Hu and Sereni. The supremum of $\mathrm{ch}_f^s(G)-\mathrm{ch}(G)$ is at least $1/7$ over planar graphs of choice number three, and at least $1/3$ over graphs of choice number $k$ for each $k\ge4$. Finally, for every sufficiently large integer $k$, we construct a graph $G$ with $\mathrm{ch}(G)=k$ that is not $(2k+t,2)$-choosable, where $t\ge C\sqrt{k}$ for an absolute constant $C>0$. Thus the gap is unbounded even with multiplicity fixed at two. We further obtain $k+Ω(\sqrt{k})\le\sup\{\mathrm{ch}_f^s(G):\mathrm{ch}(G)=k\}\le2^{(1+o(1))k}$ as $k$ tends to infinity.

items.title: On the stable birational type of Fano threefolds
items.summary: We show that, given a very general cubic threefold $X$, any smooth cubic threefold stably birational to $X$ must be isomorphic to $X$. The method applies as well to other Fano 3-folds, like the sextic double solid, and the quartic threefold. We also discuss the higher-dimensional case.

items.title: The generator problem for C*-algebras with comparison
items.summary: We show that certain classes of unital, simple, separable C*-algebras with comparison are singly generated, including tracially AF algebras and monotracial crossed products of actions on the Cantor space. In particular, we show that simple, separable, tracially AF algebras have generator rank one.

items.title: Scott spectra of distributive continuous lattices
items.summary: Let \(L\) be a distributive continuous lattice. We prove that the hull--kernel topology on \(\Spec(L)\) is the Scott topology of the inclusion order if and only if \(σ(L^{\op})=\upsilon(L^{\op})\). The necessary implication and the algebraic case are known. We prove sufficiency for arbitrary distributive continuous lattices, thereby obtaining the spectrum characterization requested by Lawson and Mislove. The proof embeds \(L\) into a continuous lattice that is both a frame and a coframe, and transfers the Scott topology of the spectrum along the induced map of spectra.

items.title: Planarity estimates and classification of ancient flows at the Andrews-Baker threshold
items.summary: We study space-time proper ancient solutions of the mean curvature flow of $n$-dimensional submanifolds of $\mathbb R^{n+p}$ that are uniformly quadratically pinched up to the Andrews-Baker threshold $\frac{4}{3n}$. We prove codimension reduction and convexity: every such solution is either a static affine $n$-plane, or a flow of hypersurfaces of a fixed affine $(n+1)$-dimensional subspace whose time slices bound convex bodies. By results of Bourni, Langford and Lynch and of Bamler and Lai, the flow is then noncollapsed, and it is a family of shrinking spheres or cylinders, an ancient oval, a bowl soliton or a flying wing, possibly times a Euclidean factor. Space-time properness replaces the finite entropy and polynomial curvature growth assumptions of Lee, Naff and Zhu. The main tool is a parabolically scale-invariant interior planarity estimate for $n\geq5$, obtained from Naff's gradient estimates through a localization argument in the spirit of Ecker and Huisken. In dimensions five and six, where these estimates do not give the gradient terms a sign, we bound them from below as in a previous work. The same localization, applied to the gradient estimate of Lynch and Nguyen and to a second order analogue, gives the derivative bounds from which convexity follows. For closed flows, we extend Lynch's planarity estimate to a larger range of exponents.

items.title: Stationary integral cycles asymptotic to a pair of transverse oriented $n$-planes at infinity
items.summary: Let $P, Q$ be two oriented transverse $n$-planes in $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$, $n\geq 2$, which satisfy the equality in the Lawlor--Nance angle criterion. We prove that any stationary integral $n$-cycle in $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$ with $[P]+[Q]$ being the tangent cone at infinity, in both the current and varifold senses, is a translation of $[P]+[Q]$ or of a Lawlor neck.

items.title: Monodromy and vanishing cycles for complete intersection curves
items.summary: We compute the topological monodromy of every family of complete intersection curves. Like in the case of plane curves previously treated by the second-named author, we find the answer is given by the $r$-spin mapping class group associated to the maximal root of the adjoint line bundle. Our main innovation is a suite of tools for studying the monodromy of sections of a tensor product of very ample line bundles in terms of the monodromy of sections of the factors, allowing for an induction on (multi-)degree.

items.title: Regularity of $Q$-valued $C^1$ harmonic functions with applications to stable minimal hypersurfaces
items.summary: We show that the derivative of a $Q$-valued $C^1$ function on an $n$-dimensional domain that is locally harmonic on its regular set is locally Dirichlet minimising, and that its branch set coincides with that of its derivative. As a consequence, we get that a $Q$-valued $C^1$ harmonic function is $C^{1,α}$ and that its branch set is countably $(n-2)$-rectifiable when $n\geq 3$ and discrete when $n=2$. Our methods are directly applicable to the regularity theory of stable minimal hypersurfaces. We show that a multi-valued Lipschitz function whose graph is a two-sided, properly immersed, stable minimal $n$-dimensional hypersurface with locally $\mathcal{H}^{n-2}$-finite singular set, and whose Lipschitz constant is sufficiently small is in fact multi-valued $C^{1,α}$. As a consequence, we obtain optimal regularity conclusions for a branched sheeting theorem of Bellettini for singular immersions. When $n=2$, we obtain stronger conclusions and show that locally about a branch point, a $Q$-valued $C^1$ harmonic function is the real part of a Dirichlet minimiser which is itself obtained from a finite number of holomorphic functions via classical branching, thus giving a full series expansion for the function near the branch point. Furthermore, we prove that the class of branched, two-sided, properly immersed, stable minimal surfaces with isolated singularities is compact under varifold convergence.

items.title: Arcs on rational double points in arbitrary characteristic
items.summary: We settle the Nash problem for two-dimensional rational double points in all characteristics. The proof is based on a direct computation of the families of arcs through these singularities.

items.title: Bi-Hamiltonian structure and conserved quantities of the Yajima-Oikawa-Newell system
items.summary:
We study the Hamiltonian and bi-Hamiltonian structure of the Yajima-Oikawa-Newell (YON) system, an integrable model of long wave-short wave interaction depending on two real parameters $α$ and $β$, which reduces to the Yajima-Oikawa system for $α=0$ and to the Newell system for $β=0$. For $α
eq0$, a constant shift of the long wave maps the YON system into the Newell system, for which two nonlocal Hamiltonian operators are known. We show that, for $α
eq0$, the system admits no local Hamiltonian operator homogeneous in its natural grading and polynomial in $β$. A nonlocal gauge transformation built on the potential of the long wave makes the first of the known operators local for a single value of its parameter: the transformed system is Hamiltonian, for every $α
eq0$ and every $β$, with respect to a local, non-degenerate Poisson operator, which is the Lie-Poisson structure of the $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$ current algebra. From a recursion operator advancing the hierarchy by two steps, given in explicit weakly nonlocal form, we construct a second, weakly nonlocal Hamiltonian structure, whose nonlocal tail is generated by the three autonomous Lie point symmetries of the system, and prove that both structures are compatible. Since the recursion operator admits no square root and the first structure has no Casimirs, the Lenard-Magri chain splits into two families, seeded by the two simplest conserved quantities. Every flow of both families is local, and all the corresponding Hamiltonians are in involution. As by-products, we relate the Lie point symmetries of the system to its conserved quantities via Noether's theorem, and obtain the conserved densities in closed form by asymptotic diagonalisation of the Lax pair.

items.title: Scattering thresholds for the NLS equation with polynomially decaying damping
items.summary: We study the focusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation with a linear damping of strength $a(1+t)^{-θ}$, where $a>0$ and $θ\ge0$, in the whole energy-subcritical range. For $θ>0$, the time-averaged damping vanishes, so that the scattering theory developed in our previous work does not apply. We show that the long-time dynamics is governed by the time integrability of an effective coupling, which decays faster than any power when $θ<1$, polynomially when $θ=1$, and not at all when $θ>1$. In the mass-subcritical case, all solutions are global. They scatter when $θ<1$ and, for $θ=1$, above an explicit exponent depending on $a$. On the other hand, no non-trivial solution is asymptotically free below a second explicit exponent when $θ=1$, and below the short-range exponent $1+2/N$ when $θ>1$. In the mass-critical case, solutions are global below the ground state. Moreover, for $θ\le1$, every solution which survives until its decaying mass becomes subcritical is global and scatters. In the intercritical case, we prove small data scattering and, for $θ\le1$, a dichotomy between scattering and grow-up of the gradient. Finally, in the scale-invariant case $θ=1$, we analyze the range between the two thresholds. We reduce the equation exactly to a nonlinear Schrödinger equation with a decaying repulsive harmonic potential, and we construct approximate solitary waves with an integrable error. This leads to a conjecture, supported by numerical simulations, on the sharpness of the scattering threshold.

items.title: Mirror symmetry for gCICY threefolds (I): a $[3,-1]$ block and a non-Gorenstein toric phase
items.summary: We construct and analyze a mirror family for the generalized complete intersection Calabi-Yau threefold $X_+=[\mathbb{P}^1\,|\,3\ {-1};\ \mathbb{P}^4\,|\,2\ 3]$, with $(h^{1,1},h^{2,1})=(2,46)$. We introduce auxiliary variables to obtain a toric GIT presentation with two chambers. The first gives $X_+$, while the second gives a Calabi-Yau threefold $X_-$ related to $X_+$ by a flop of 16 disjoint $(-1,-1)$-curves. The threefold $X_-$ is a nef complete intersection in a non-Gorenstein toric $\mathbb{Q}$-Fano eightfold. Then the Hori-Vafa equations give a 2-parameter Laurent family, and we construct a smooth projective crepant model $Y$ of its general member with mirrored Hodge numbers. The rank-6 Picard-Fuchs system of $Y$ has two maximally unipotent boundary points, whose indicial algebras are isomorphic to the even cohomology rings $H^{\mathrm{even}}(X_+,\mathbb{C})$ and $H^{\mathrm{even}}(X_-,\mathbb{C})$. We also show that the predicted genus-zero BPS numbers of the first two vertical degrees agree with direct counts of lines and conics on the genus-one fibration $X_-\to\mathbb{P}^2$.

items.title: Canonical Volumes of Threefolds with Positive Geometric Genus
items.summary: We prove that a complex projective threefold of general type with canonical singularities and positive geometric genus has canonical volume at least $1/30$, with strict inequality when its Euler characteristic is positive. We describe the equality cases as canonical hypersurfaces of degree $28$ in $\mathbb P(1,3,4,5,14)$. These canonical models and their smooth projective resolutions are simply connected. Their coarse moduli space is irreducible and rational of dimension $103$, with finite quotient singularities; all admissible $\mathbb Q$-Gorenstein deformations are unobstructed and arise by varying the equation.

items.title: The strongly local part of nonlinear Dirichlet structures and its energy measures
items.summary: This paper substantially extends the results of Sasaya (2026, JFA): we propose a framework for nonlinear generalizations of regular Dirichlet forms and prove that each energy in this framework has a largest strongly local part. We also prove the existence and uniqueness of canonical energy measures of this part, which satisfy convexity and locality properties and, under additional assumptions, certain chain rules in one variable. In particular, our framework requires neither $p$-homogeneity nor strong locality. Moreover, under a Ball--Carlen--Lieb-type upper bound, we prove more detailed chain rules for the directional derivatives of these energy measures. Our framework is applicable both to $p$-energy forms on fractals and to a class of symmetric nonlinear Dirichlet forms in the sense of Cipriani and Grillo~\cite{CG2003}, including those of Orlicz--Sobolev and variable-exponent Sobolev type.

items.title: Long-time behaviour of solutions for equations with randomness
items.summary: We discuss results on the mixing properties of solutions for discrete and continuous time equations, drived by stationary bounded random forces, obtained during the last three years in a number or our joint papers. To facilitate applications of these results to specific equations with randomness, the results are edited and properly re-arranged.

items.title: On operators with infinitely many spectral components
items.summary: For a unital complex Banach algebra $\mathscr A$ and $n\in\mathbb N$, let $\mathcal C_n(\mathscr A)$ be the set of all elements whose spectrum has at least $n$ connected components, and let $\mathcal C_\infty(\mathscr A)=\bigcap_{n\in\mathbb N}\mathcal C_n(\mathscr A)$. We prove that $\mathcal C_\infty(\mathscr A)\neq\varnothing$ if and only if $\mathscr A$ contains a sequence of non-zero pairwise orthogonal idempotents, and that the number of components of a spectrum is always finite, $\aleph_0$ or $\mathfrak c$. This allows us to extend the spectral depth $d_σ(\mathscr A)$ to a cardinal-valued invariant with values in $\mathbb N\cup\{\aleph_0,\mathfrak c\}$. We show that $d_σ(\mathscr A)=\mathfrak c$ precisely when $\mathscr A$ contains a dyadic family of idempotents indexed by the full binary tree. In that case, some element has spectrum homeomorphic to the Cantor space $\mathbf 2^{\mathbb N}$. The supremum defining $d_σ(\mathscr A)$ is attained when the spectral classes of $\mathscr A$ are dense and when $\mathscr A$ is commutative, but not in general. We construct a unital complex Banach algebra with $d_σ(\mathscr A)=\aleph_0$ and $\mathcal C_\infty(\mathscr A)=\varnothing$. If $Δ$ is the character space of a commutative $\mathscr A$ and $π_0(Δ)$ is the space of all components of $Δ$, then $d_σ(\mathscr A)=\card\bigl(π_0(Δ)\bigr)$ when $π_0(Δ)$ is finite, $d_σ(\mathscr A)=\aleph_0$ when $π_0(Δ)$ is infinite and scattered, and $d_σ(\mathscr A)=\mathfrak c$ when $π_0(Δ)$ is not scattered. We also prove that the spectral depth is additive with respect to finite direct sums and that the spectral classes are invariant under injective holomorphic functions.

items.title: Cost controllability and predictive control of input-constrained monotone systems on Hilbert spaces
items.summary: Cost controllability, relating controllability and a performance measure like the stage cost in model predictive control (MPC), is a key tool in the stability and suboptimality analysis of closed-loop systems. We establish cost controllability for maximal monotone control systems subject to input constraints, a class encompassing finite- and infinite-dimensional port-Hamiltonian systems with colocated input and output. To this end, we employ a recently proposed saturated feedback to derive state-dependent bounds on the closed-loop cost. Our main result is that cost controllability holds globally with semiglobal exponential rate. We first establish this result in continuous time and then extend it to sampled-data systems. Whereas a qualitative detectability-like property is sufficient for asymptotic convergence of the controller, cost controllability requires quantitative rates. We provide two verifiable conditions ensuring cost controllability with explicit exponential rates: coercivity of the sum of system operator and output injection, and exponential detectability of the linear part. Moreover, under the coercivity condition, the resulting MPC scheme without terminal conditions renders the equilibrium globally asymptotically stable with semiglobal exponential rate already for prediction horizon two. We illustrate our results by a nonlinear finite-dimensional system, a semilinear heat equation and a nonlinearly damped wave equation.

items.title: Phragmén-Lindelöf theorems for parabolic equations of p-laplacian-type
items.summary: We consider rigidity properties of ancient solutions to parabolic equations of $p$-Laplacian-type. We start with the degenerate range $p>2$. First, a solution which is bounded above in an intrinsic backward paraboloid is either bounded in an entire half-space, or grows in space at least like a power with a sharp, explicit exponent. This relies on the expansion of positivity and on the Comparison Principle. Then, we turn to the growth in time. Positivity in the paraboloid alone yields no upper rate: we present explicit self-similar solutions, positive in the paraboloid, with $u(0,-T)\simeq T^β$ for every $β\le0$ and every $β\ge1$. For solutions bounded below in the paraboloid, we prove a dichotomy for the infimum of $u(\cdot,-T)$ on a ball whose radius is a fixed fraction of that of the paraboloid at time $-T$: either it is of order $T$ along a sequence of times, or it grows sublinearly, like $T^ζ$ with $ζ<1$ explicit. In the second case, a Harnack-type argument shows that the supremum on the same ball grows at most linearly. Then, we carry out the same program in the singular, supercritical range $\frac{2N}{N+1}<p<2$, where the picture is similar but several roles are reversed. In space, the iteration via the Comparison Principle can only be started from a point lying above an explicit slope, and explicit solutions show that nothing better than a cone bound can be expected below it. The self-similar profiles are unique but only local, and positivity in the paraboloid is compatible with every exponent $β\le1$ and with no exponent in $(1,\frac1{2-p})$. In time, the dichotomy is replaced by an a priori linear bound for the infimum. Similarities and differences between the two ranges are collected at the end of the work.

items.title: Timelike Supersymmetric Geometries in Seven-Dimensional Supergravity
items.summary: Seven-dimensional supergravity poses a uniquely intricate supersymmetry problem, combining topologically massive higher-form gauge dynamics, distinct Clifford algebra properties, and rich geometric structures. We first establish the complete formulation of the maximal Cartan-gauged theory in terms of the gauge-invariant higher-form flux, including both the bosonic action and supersymmetry variations. This formulation, which also makes the smooth ungauged limit manifest, is achieved by requiring a consistent truncation to the minimal Cartan-gauged theory in the equal-charge limit. We construct the complete bilinear system for a timelike Killing vector, where additional internal orientation of the symplectic-Majorana spinor arises already in the scalar sector, uniquely among pure minimal ungauged theories. In the equal-charge sector, we decouple the algebraic constraints into SU$(3)$-isotypic components, and analyse the differential bilinear relations, determining the permitted dilaton gradient, fluxes, fibration twist and intrinsic torsion of the base. We prove that with gauging and active Cartan flux, the complex scalar bilinear vanishes identically. We also construct a Killing gauge for the higher-form potential compatible with the self-duality condition. We show that with gauging but no active Cartan flux, the Killing vector also acts as a generator of the gauged R-symmetry, and the base structure is enlarged from SU$(3)$ to U$(3)$. We find that BPS-flow solutions realize this setting. With supersymmetry, we isolate a single independent component of the 3-form equation across an exhaustive four-class partition for both theories within this setup. Applied to known and proposed solutions in both theories, this classification exposes unexplored sectors and provides an accessible toolbox for constructing and testing solutions and developing new geometric and holographic applications.

items.title: Pseudoconformal characterizations of scattering in weighted Sobolev spaces for non-scaling-invariant mass-subcritical NLS
items.summary: We consider mass-subcritical nonlinear Schrödinger equations with finitely many power-type nonlinearities and initial data in weighted Sobolev spaces. In the short-range regime, we prove a pseudoconformal characterization of scattering in the weighted energy space $Σ$. We also establish a fractional counterpart in $Σ^s$, $s\in(0,1)$, formulated in terms of the boundedness of the order-$s$ pseudoconformal operator. Our results include equations with combined nonlinearities, for which no distinguished scaling symmetry is available. As an application of the fractional theory, we prove small-data scattering in $Σ^s$, $s\in(0,1]$. The arguments rely on the lens transformation, harmonic-oscillator Strichartz estimates, and fractional harmonic Sobolev estimates.

items.title: The inradius law for the cavities of planar Brownian motion, with applications to the Wiener sausage
items.summary: ```text Let $K_1=B[0,1]$ be the trace of a planar Brownian motion, and let $N_{\mathrm{in}}(η)$ be the number of its cavities, the bounded components of $\mathbb{R}^2\setminus K_1$, whose inradius exceeds $η$. We prove that, almost surely and in $L^p$ for every $p\in[1,2]$, $η^2(\log(1/η))^2 N_{\mathrm{in}}(η)\to c_{\mathrm{in}}=\fracπ{2}\int G^2 d\mathcal{L}\in(0,\frac12]$, where $G$ is the ratio of the inradius of a shape to the square root of its area and $\mathcal{L}$ is Werner's limiting shape law. The inradius, and not the area by which the cavities have been counted classically, decides survival under thickening: a cavity contains a hole of the Wiener sausage of radius $r$ if and only if its inradius exceeds $r$. Through Brownian scaling, the number $β_1^T(r)$ of holes of the sausage of radius $r$ of $B[0,T]$, the Betti curve of its degree-one persistent homology, is bounded below at the scale $T/(r^2(\log T)^2)$, with the identified constant $4c_{\mathrm{in}}$ in expectation and with any smaller constant with probability tending to one. A matching upper bound cannot follow from any general bound in terms of perimeter, area, diameter or length; we prove that it is equivalent to a first-moment estimate for near-critical pockets, the holes at level $η$ on which the distance to the trace is at most $2η$. That estimate is proved in a companion paper, so that the expected number of holes is of exact order $T/(r^2(\log T)^2)$. ```

items.title: On the topology of some linear systems of hyperelliptic curves in Hirzebruch surfaces
items.summary: Following a program suggested by Dolgachev and Libgober in 1981, we study the topology of the locus of smooth sections of linear systems of hyperelliptic curves on Hirzebruch surfaces. Our primary interest is the computation of various flavors of ``enriched monodromy representations''. Within this class of examples, we find that a variety of behaviors occur - in some situations the enriched monodromy faithfully captures the fundamental group, and in others it does not. Our arguments mainly leverage algebro-geometric techniques to compute cohomological obstructions to families of embeddings.

items.title: List coloring uncrowded hypergraphs at the shattering threshold
items.summary: A foundational theorem of Ajtai, Komlós, Pintz, Spencer, and Szemerédi asserts that every $n$-vertex $k$-uniform uncrowded hypergraph (i.e., with girth at least $5$) of maximum degree at most $Δ$ contains an independent set of size $cn(\logΔ/Δ)^{\frac{1}{k-1}}$ for some absolute constant $c>0$. Improving an earlier bound of Frieze and Mubayi, Iliopoulos showed that every such hypergraph has list chromatic number at most $(1+o(1))(k-1)(Δ/\logΔ)^{\frac{1}{k-1}}$. Determining the optimal leading constant in this bound remains a major open problem. A natural target, suggested by the coupon-collector heuristic, is $(k-1)^{\frac{1}{k-1}}$, which also corresponds to the shattering threshold for coloring sparse random hypergraphs. Our main result shows that this target is attained: for every integer $k\ge2$, every $k$-uniform uncrowded hypergraph of maximum degree at most $Δ$ satisfies: $$χ_\ell(\mathcal{H})\le(1+o(1))\Big((k-1)\fracΔ{\logΔ}\Big)^{\frac{1}{k-1}}.$$ In particular, this confirms a 2019 conjecture of Molloy for uncrowded hypergraphs. Building on this result, we prove that every $k$-uniform linear hypergraph of maximum degree at most $Δ$ has chromatic number at most $(c_k+o(1))(Δ/\logΔ)^{\frac{1}{k-1}}$, where $c_k\to1$ as $k\to\infty$, thereby proving a conjecture of Verstraëte and Wilson on the independence number of linear hypergraphs in the stronger form of colorings. Our techniques also yield a palette sparsification theorem for uncrowded hypergraphs, partially answering a question of Casselgren and Eriksson.

items.title: Bernoulli flow for Erdős-Rényi graphs
items.summary: We study the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the adjacency matrix $A$ of the Erdős-Rényi graph $\mathbb G(N,p)$ in the regime $Np \gg (\log N)^2$. We establish optimal isotropic delocalization for the bulk eigenvectors $\boldsymbol u$, meaning that $\langle \boldsymbol v, \boldsymbol u\rangle^2 \leq \frac{C \log N}{N}$ with very high probability for any deterministic normalized $\boldsymbol v$. In addition, we prove local spectral universality in the bulk by showing that the local spectral statistics coincide with those of the GOE. The main tool of our proof is a local law for the resolvent of $A$, down to optimal spectral scales and with optimal error bounds. Its proof relies on a new approach to local laws that we call the Bernoulli flow. It is a characteristic flow method in which the usual Brownian process is replaced by a Bernoulli process, where each edge of the graph forms an independent Markov process that jumps at unit rate from closed to open. The spectral parameter flows according to a suitably constructed matrix-valued Bernoulli characteristic flow.

items.title: Tolerance complexes of chordal graphs and squarefree symbolic powers
items.summary: For a simplicial complex $K$ and an integer $t\ge0$, the $t$-tolerance complex $\mathcal{T}_t(K)$ consists of the sets that become faces of $K$ after deleting at most $t$ of their elements. Kim and Lew conjectured that if $K$ is $d$-Leray, then $\mathcal{T}_t(K)$ is $(η(d+1,t+1)-1)$-Leray (the Leray conjecture), and that if $K$ is $d$-collapsible, then $\mathcal{T}_t(K)$ is $(η(d+1,t+1)-1)$-collapsible (the collapsibility conjecture), where $η$ is the Erdős--Gallai number. We prove the collapsibility conjecture for $d=1$ when $t\le3$ or $\dim K\le4$, and for all $t$ when $K$ is the clique complex of a subtree graph of a spider, a class of chordal graphs containing all interval and split graphs; in particular, it holds for nerves of finite families of intervals. For every $d$, we prove both conjectures when $K$ has at most $d+1$ facets, when $K$ has nonzero homology in its top dimension, and when the Stanley--Reisner ideal of $K$ is squarefree stable. The Stanley--Reisner ideal of $\mathcal{T}_t(K)$ is the $(t+1)$-st squarefree symbolic power of that of $K$, so the Leray conjecture becomes a regularity bound. Using this, we prove the Leray conjecture for flag complexes when $t\le3$, and for all $t$ for independence complexes of bipartite and chordal graphs, and we show that it is preserved under joins. We also construct chordal graphs $H$ for which the Leray number of $\mathcal{T}_t(\mathrm{Cl}(H))$ exceeds its Helly dimension by an arbitrarily large amount, and others for which it depends on the field. Finally, we reduce the case $t=1$ of the Leray bound for $d$-collapsible complexes to a question on intersections of links.

items.title: Khovanov and knot Floer homology of fibered positive links
items.summary: For fibered positive links, we compute the reduced and unreduced Khovanov homology in homological grading two over both $\mathbb{Z}$ and $\mathbb{F}_2$, and the knot Floer homology in the penultimate Alexander grading. Our Khovanov calculations, combined with the result of Przytycki-Sazdanović, prove that every nontrivial semi-adequate knot has 2-torsion in its unreduced Khovanov homology. This establishes Shumakovitch's conjecture for semi-adequate knots, which include all nontrivial positive knots. The proofs involve induction using the skein exact sequences, with the Hopf link as the base case.

items.title: Vietoris-Rips complexes of affine Coxeter groups
items.summary: We prove that all affine Coxeter groups admit contractible Vietoris-Rips complexes. More precisely, for any affine Coxeter group $W_a$ with standard generating set $S$, we prove that the Vietoris-Rips complex $\mathcal{VR}_t(W_a;S)$ is contractible for all sufficiently large $t$. We also investigate other finitely generated groups of the form $G=H\rtimes F$ for $F$ finite, and prove that for any finite symmetric generating set $A$ for $H$ such that $A^F=A$, the complexes $\mathcal{VR}_t(G;AF)$ and $\mathcal{VR}_t(H;A)$ are homotopy equivalent for all $t\ge 1$.

items.title: Scattering of the defocusing Calogero--Moser derivative nonlinear Schrödinger equation
items.summary: In this paper, we study the long time behavior of solutions to the defocusing Calogero--Moser derivative nonlinear Schrödinger equation (CM-DNLS). Using the Gérard-type explicit formula, we prove the scattering result of solutions to this equation with initial data in $L_{+}^2(\mathbb{R}):=\left\{f \in L^2(\mathbb{R}): \operatorname{supp}(\widehat{f}) \subset[0,+\infty)\right\}$. We also characterize the scattering term using the distorted Fourier transform associated with the Lax operator. This is one of the first works that apply the Gérard-type explicit formula to study the long-time behavior of an integrable equation for a broad class of initial data, beyond the previously studied rational cases.

items.title: Block-exchange descent for insertion: commuting projections and minimum masks
items.summary: For fixed nonempty words $u,v$, the minimum insertion degree of a shuffle is the least number of inserted-source runs among its representations. We prove that, after a block exchange from a minimum mask of degree $r$, the minimum over masks with commuting source projections is exactly $r-1$; a larger decrease occurs precisely when a noncommuting mask has fewer runs. If either source is unary, every such exchange is exact. We prove an explicit repair for an infinite periodic degree-three family. Computer-assisted results establish first-mask descent through combined length seventeen over every alphabet, degree-three first-mask descent through length thirty, and a uniform repair of all degree-three failures through length thirty, including all further letter identifications. Counterexamples to arbitrary, first, and last minimum-mask choices explain the need for alternative masks. Finally, we prove that minimum iteration depths have no gaps for arbitrary languages. General block-exchange descent and Singleton No-Gap remain open.

items.title: Parabolic semiinfinite sheaves on affine flag varieties
items.summary: We study sheaves on affine flag varieties of reductive algebraic groups in parabolic semiinfinite settings, generalizing some constructions and results from the work of Gaitsgory and of Achar, Dhillon, and the first author (for the case of the Borel subgroup) and of Dhillon and Lysenko (for characteristic-$0$ coefficients and a particular case of parabolic semiinfinite condition). In particular we define perverse t-structures and Raskin equivalences in this context, and study an analogue of the Gaitsgory sheaf. In future work, these $\infty$-categories will be related to representation-theoretic $\infty$-categories associated with the Langlands dual group.

items.title: From Distribution of Extremes With Degradation to the Stress Redundancy Principle
items.summary: How a degradation source affects the statistics of the first among many identical independent stochastic particles to successfully reach a narrow target remains unclear. Here, we investigate the impact of degradation on the distributions of first-passage times and exit locations by exploiting the time-dependent fluxes associated with the corresponding Fokker-Planck equation. We also compute the escape probability by solving a mixed boundary value problem. In the large initial population $N_0$ limit, we derive an asymptotic formula for the mean first passage time associated with the fastest particle, revealing how the killing field modifies the classical $1/\log(N_0)$ scaling. However, when considering the population size at the time of the first exit, we obtain a specific dependency with respect to degradation, a phenomenon that we call the stress redundancy principle. For a degradation field restricted to a narrow subregion, we use an optimal control approach to derive the optimal trajectory where the fastest escape particles will be concentrated: interestingly, we report here that the optimal trajectories avoid the degradation area depending on killing intensity. Finally, we obtain analytical expressions for the distribution of first exit points along a narrow absorbing arc in two-dimensional regular domains. In addition, for a killing subregion tangent to the target boundary, our computations reveal how geometrical parameters influence the exit distribution. In summary, a killing source can significantly affect the statistics of the fastest diffusing particles, relevant for defining cellular and molecular time scales.

items.title: No 13-vertex triangulation of the three-torus
items.summary: Kühnel and Lassmann constructed a neighborly triangulation of the three-torus on 15 vertices, and Lutz conjectured that it is vertex-minimal. The standard lower-bound arguments exclude at most twelve vertices but do not decide the 13- and 14-vertex cases. We exclude the 13-vertex case. Our proof uses the Novik--Swartz $g_2$-inequality and a simplicial-complement reduction to a nine-vertex model of the punctured three-torus. By analyzing fundamental groups of small simplicial complexes and applying Alexander duality in a vertex link, we obtain a contradiction from the deficiency of $\Z^3$.

items.title: Independent Families Under Determinacy-Like Hypotheses
items.summary: We generalize the notion of an independent family on $ω$ to $\mathcal{J}$-independent families on an arbitrary cardinal $κ$ and then show that under determinacy-like hypotheses that there can be no such families for reasonable $\mathcal{J}$. This is quite atypical as all other generalizations of the kinds of combinatorial families coming from the theory of cardinal characteristics follow a very different pattern, which will also be explained; in this sense independent families seem particularly special. The base theory assumed throughout is $\textsf{ZF + }$All infinite sets are Dedekind infinite.

items.title: Nonproduct Minimal Submanifolds with Cylindrical Tangent Cones
items.summary: This article constructs, via perturbation methods, infinite-dimensional families of non-product minimal submanifolds which have singular sets locally modeled on cylindrical tangent cones. This answers a question raised by Leon Simon in the 1980s, and generalizes work Caffarelli-Hardt-Simon, who treated the case of isolated singularities. This setting requires substantially more work, however, since the natural obstruction space for the problem is infinite dimensional and the map which is meant to compensate for this obstruction using deformations of the singular set exhibits a loss of regularity. This necessitates working in the category of tame Frechet spaces and using the Nash-Moser Implicit Function Theorem.

items.title: Trefftz DG Approximation of the T-Matrix for Scattering by Periodic Layered Structures
items.summary: We study the scattering of time-harmonic electromagnetic waves by periodic layered gratings, modelled by the 2D Helmholtz equation. The periodic obstacle may include penetrable and impenetrable regions, and consists of a finite number of stacked layers. The boundary value problem is formulated on a single periodic cell using quasi-periodic boundary conditions. The radiation condition in the vertical directions is imposed through Dirichlet-to-Neumann (DtN) operators. To efficiently treat multilayer configurations, we adopt a formulation based on the T-matrix method. The global scattering problem is decomposed into boundary value problems posed on individual layers. On the layer boundaries, the field is expressed in terms of quasi-periodic modal expansions, and the layer T-matrix describes the map between incoming and outgoing wave modes. Each local T-matrix is approximated numerically using a plane-wave based Trefftz Discontinuous Galerkin (TDG) method, which provides an efficient discretization of the layer scattering response. The T-matrix technique leads to linear computational complexity in the number of layers in the grating.

items.title: Computing Lower Bounds on the Nonnegative Rank via Non-Convex Optimization Solvers
items.summary: The nonnegative rank of a nonnegative matrix $X$ is the smallest number of nonnegative rank-one factors that sum to $X$. Since computing the nonnegative rank is NP-hard, it is common to circumvent this issue by computing lower and upper bounds. In this paper, we propose non-convex formulations and practical implementations for four important lower bounds for the nonnegative rank, namely the fooling set bound (FSB), the rectangle covering bound (RCB), the hyperplane separation bound (HSB), and the self-scaled bound (SSB). In particular, to the best of our knowledge, our algorithm for computing the SSB is the first available in the literature. We compute the SSB for several matrices for which its value had not previously been reported. In some cases, the SSB provides the best known upper bound, while the other three bounds do not. Moreover, on canonical benchmarks, we show that our non-convex approaches are often competitive with existing methods. The paper also provides a consolidated reference for the current state of several classical lower bounds on a large number of benchmark matrices.

items.title: The Symplectic Nature of Noncentral Reducible Stratum in SU(2) Character Variety
items.summary: Let \(Σ_g\) be a closed oriented surface of genus \(g\geq2\). The purpose of this paper is to use an explicit example, the representation of the surface group $π_1(Σ_g)$ into $\mathrm{SU}(2)$, to investigate the deformation space of the representation variety at a type of singular points, reducible but noncentral representations, and explore the geometric structure of the corresponding stratum in the representation variety and the character variety. In particular, the reduced tangent quadratic cone determines the symplectic structure at the reducible noncentral stratum of the character variety. Such a symplectic structure fits in the ambient character variety $χ\big(π_1(Σ_g),\mathrm{SU}(2)\big)$, where the top stratum of smooth points admits the Narasimhan-Atiyah-Bott-Goldman symplectic structure.

items.title: Shape Perturbation of the Galerkin Boundary Element Dirichlet-to-Neumann Matrix on Moving Polygons
items.summary: For nonlocal interface evolution problems such as the Mullins-Sekerka flow, certain parametric schemes discretize only the interface and approximate the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map by boundary elements. Their error analysis requires bounds on how this discrete operator changes as the polygon moves. In that analysis, the polygons are only Lipschitz and close to a smooth curve only in a Lipschitz norm, the perturbations are controlled only in the energy norm, and the kernels are singular on the diagonal. We study the symmetric Galerkin boundary element matrix on the polygons in a Lipschitz neighborhood of a smooth reference curve. Its first variation, tested against discrete Neumann solutions, is bounded by the energy norm of the perturbation alone. The second-order remainder of the associated mass form is bounded by the product of the energy norm and the Lipschitz norm of the perturbation, so that only one of the two factors needs a uniform bound. On the interpolating polygon, the matrix is consistent with the continuous operator without the logarithmic loss that a pointwise comparison of the kernels would suggest, and its shape derivative is consistent with that of the continuous operator. All bounds are uniform in the mesh size and depend only on the constants of the reference curve.

items.title: Splitting module-finite extensions over singular local rings
items.summary: We study when a module-finite extension of a singular local ring splits as a module over the base. On a Gorenstein curve of positive residue characteristic, weak normality forces splitting for every extension of finite projective dimension. In residue characteristic two the converse holds when two is zero or a nonzerodivisor. A missing square root in the prescribed base gives an explicit nonsplit extension of generic rank four. We obtain a second curve criterion by gluing retractions on the branches and determine all evaluation ideals for coordinate crossings and for \(x^2=y^2u z_1\cdots z_s\) in odd characteristic. For cubic extensions we prove a presentation theorem with arbitrarily many relations. It applies on the blow-up of an ideal generated by a regular sequence of length three, and on the blow-up of a three-dimensional local ring with a quadric tangent cone. A family of matrices satisfying the criterion exists over every residue field in the regular-sequence case.

items.title: Generalized Cramér-Rao Inequalities Associated with $(h,τ)$-Divergence and $(h,τ)$-Exponential Family
items.summary: The Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence and exponential family have laid the foundation for information geometry and have been widely generalized. Using Eguchi's theory, the Fisher information metric can be derived from the KL divergence. Based on this metric, Amari and Nagaoka established an information-geometric proof of the classical Cramér-Rao (CR) inequality for finite-support models. Among the various generalizations of the KL divergence, this paper focuses on the $(h,τ)$-divergence and establishes the associated CR inequality, referred to as the $(h,τ)$-CR inequality, using information geometry. We also provide a proof of this inequality based on the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, thereby extending its applicability to models with more general support sets. Under suitable regularity conditions, equality holds in the classical CR inequality if and only if the underlying family is exponential. However, for the $(h,τ)$-CR inequality, this property does not generally extend to the $(h,τ)$-exponential family. We therefore establish an attainable CR inequality for this family. This new inequality extends the attainment result of the classical CR inequality by the sufficient statistic of the exponential family to the $(h,τ)$-exponential family.

items.title: Smoothed Least-Absolute Conditional Multidimensional Scaling via Iteratively Reweighted Majorization
items.summary: Conditional multidimensional scaling combines latent coordinates with observed covariates to fit pairwise dissimilarities. We develop a smoothed l1 formulation using the shifted Charbonnier loss. We prove residualwise sharpness of the quadratic loss majorizer, monotonicity, compact containment, and stationarity of noncollapsed accumulation points. A uniform additive bound quantifies approximation to exact least-absolute conditional stress. The experiments use paired contamination, separately calibrated loss parameters, combined-configuration recovery, and direct checks of the theorem's inequalities.

items.title: Affine Tracing: A New Paradigm for Probabilistic Linear Solvers
items.summary: Probabilistic linear solvers (PLSs) return probability distributions that quantify uncertainty due to limited computation in the solution of linear systems. The literature has traditionally distinguished between Bayesian PLSs, which condition a prior on information obtained from projections of the linear system, and probabilistic iterative methods (PIMs), which lift classical iterative solvers to probability space. In this work we show this dichotomy to be false: Bayesian PLSs are a special case of non-stationary affine PIMs. In addition, we prove that any realistic affine PIM is calibrated. These results motivate a focus on (non-stationary) affine PIMs, but their practical adoption has been limited by the significant manual effort required to implement them. To address this, we introduce affine tracing, an algorithmic framework that automatically constructs a PIM from a standard implementation of an affine iterative method by passing symbolic tracers through the computation to build an affine computational graph. We show how this graph can be transformed to compute posterior covariances, and how equality saturation can be used to perform algebraic simplifications required for computation under specific prior choices. We demonstrate the framework by automatically generating a probabilistic multigrid solver and evaluate its performance in the context of Gaussian process approximation.

items.title: Numerical analysis of coupled flow, deformation and frictional contact mechanics in a fractured porous medium
items.summary: This paper studies the numerical approximation of a mathematical model of coupled flow and viscoelastic deformation in a fractured porous medium including fracture contact mechanics. We consider a mixed-dimensional model, where the fracture is modeled as a co-dimension one object within the porous medium. This model couples Darcy flow in the matrix and fracture, linear viscoelasticity of the matrix and frictional contact mechanics of the fracture surfaces; the contact conditions include normal compliance and a Coulomb friction law. We propose and analyze a fully discrete numerical scheme for this problem, using conformal finite elements in space and the implicit Euler method in time. Existence and uniqueness of the discrete solution is established, and stability and a priori error estimates are derived. A numerical experiment is performed in which numerical error estimates are computed and compared to the theoretical results.

items.title: Ramification of torsion packets on curves with good-reduction Jacobians
items.summary: Let $p\ge5$ be a prime number, $k$ an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$. Write $R=W(k)$ for the ring of Witt vectors over $k$, and $K$ for the field of fractions of $R$. Let $X$ be a smooth, proper, geometrically connected curve over $K$ of genus greater than one. Write $J$ for the Jacobian variety of $X$. Fix an algebraic closure $\overline{K}$ of $K$. In the present paper, we prove that if $J$ has good reduction over $R$, then every point $x\in X(\overline{K})$ such that $[σx-x]$ is torsion for each $σ\in \operatorname{Gal}(\overline{K}/K)$ is $K$-rational.

items.title: Pareto Front Tracing in Higher Dimensions Using Numerical Integration
items.summary: We propose a numerical integration approach for tracing the Pareto front of unconstrained continuous multi-objective optimization problems. By stating optimality conditions for weighted sum scalarizations, we derive parametric equations for Pareto critical points, parameterized by the weights. Sensitivity analysis with respect to the weights yields a system of partial differential equations (PDEs). We prove local existence and uniqueness of solutions and derive conditions under which a solution extends to the entire weight space and yields Pareto optimal solutions. A tracing strategy for the resulting PDE system is developed that uses numerical integration along individual weight coordinates using Runge--Kutta methods. We provide an error analysis considering inexact initial solutions, perturbations of the right-hand sides, and numerical integration errors. We investigate the accuracy and computational efficiency of the tracing strategy on convex quadratic problems and WFG examples, where the latter demonstrate the applicability to problems with Pareto fronts consisting of convex and non-convex parts. Comparisons with repeated weighted sum scalarizations and a predictor--corrector method illustrate the computational benefits of the proposed strategy.

items.title: Asymptotic Robustness of HDG Schemes for the Convection-Diffusion Equation
items.summary: The convection-diffusion problem has been studied extensively as an important model for convection-dominated problems. The problem becomes more challenging when the convecting velocity is no longer Lipschitz and merely has Sobolev regularity. In this paper, we use Boyer's extension of the DiPerna--Lions theory for the transport equation to study the vanishing diffusion limit of discretizations of the convection-diffusion equation with Sobolev velocity. In the case of flux-adapted boundary conditions, we prove that a continuous Galerkin discretization converges strongly to the renormalized solution of the transport equation as the diffusion coefficient and mesh size go to zero, without requiring any relationship between them. We refer to this unconditional strong convergence as asymptotic robustness. In the case of Dirichlet boundary conditions, we use the renormalization theory and barrier arguments to prove that a piecewise constant hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin scheme is asymptotically robust, while the continuous Galerkin scheme may fail to converge. Our results indicate that the asymptotic robustness of schemes for the convection-diffusion problem depends on the realization of the boundary conditions as opposed to internal layers.

items.title: Characterizing Fixed-Treewidth Planar Graphs
items.summary: We give the first inductive characterization of planar graphs of treewidth $k$ for each $k \geq 3$. Our definition generalizes the well-known inductive definition of planar $3$-trees and the recent definition of so-called planar quasi-$4$-trees [Förster, 2024]. As a key step, which may be of independent interest, we show that every planar triangulation $G$ of treewidth $k$ admits a tree decomposition of width $k$ where each adhesion set induces a cycle in $G$. As an application of planar quasi-$4$-trees, we show that planar graphs of treewidth at most $4$ have vertex arboricity at most $2$. That is, the vertex-set of every planar graph of treewidth at most $4$ can be partitioned into two sets that each induce a forest.

items.title: Inequivalence of the various notions of completeness for Cartan geometries
items.summary: We demonstrate that the three standard notions of completeness for Cartan geometries are not actually equivalent, modernizing and extending results due to Yeaton Clifton. In an effort to rectify the folklore on the topic, we also provide detailed explanations of how specious proofs in the literature that would claim that these types of completeness are equivalent break down. In the affine case, we construct geodesically complete homogeneous examples with an inextensible exponential curve for each connected Lie group of dimension at least 2, as well as an infinite-dimensional family of examples whose exponential curves are defined for all time but whose overlying frame bundle is not complete as a metric space with respect to a natural metric for the Cartan connection.

items.title: Bounding and Approximating Kostka Numbers
items.summary: Kostka numbers, the coefficients of Schur polynomials, count semistandard Young tableaux of prescribed shape and weight. We give a deterministic algorithm for approximating Kostka numbers within a simply exponential factor in the number of variables and the size of the partition. Our approach combines Gurvits capacity bounds for log-concave polynomials with an algorithm for approximating the Gurvits capacity of a Schur polynomial. For a Schur polynomial in $n$ variables indexed by $λ$, we show that the logarithm of the capacity associated with any nonzero coefficient can be approximated to additive error $ε$ in time polynomial in $n$, $|λ|$, and $\log(1/ε)$. The analysis establishes an explicit bounded optimization region and efficient approximate first-order oracles, and handles boundary weights through a factorization into smaller Schur polynomials.

items.title: Poisson boundaries of lattices in locally compact groups
items.summary: For a random walk on a general locally compact group we provide a discretization procedure transforming the walk to one on a lattice of the group, preserving the Poisson boundary and some finiteness of moments.

items.title: Reconstructing Numerical Semigroups from Circulant Spectral Dimensions
items.summary: The polynomial algebra generated by the spectral moments of a family of circulant graphs consists of all eventually polynomial sequences in the graph order; as an unfiltered algebra, it therefore carries little information about the jumps. We show that its natural power-sum weight filtration retains substantially finer arithmetic data. For a finite jump set $S$ with $\gcd(S)=1$ and $M=\max S$, the relevant invariant is the numerical semigroup $Σ_S=\langle M,M-s,M+s:s\in S\rangle$, which arises from the lengths of closed walks winding around the cycle. We prove that the eventual global filtered dimension is $MD+\lfloor D/2\rfloor+1-M(M+1)-g(Σ_S)$. Restricting graph orders to $n\equiv a\pmod q$, for $q\mid M$, replaces the genus term by the number of gaps of $Σ_S$ in the class $-a\pmod q$; the class $a=0$ gives the genus of the quotient semigroup $Σ_S/q$. These formulas yield an inverse reconstruction theorem: the unrestricted dimensions determine $M$, and the dimensions in all classes modulo $M$ at one common stable degree determine the Apéry set and hence $Σ_S$. We give effective thresholds, exact examples, and a finite-rank algorithm valid in every degree. Reconstruction of the semigroup need not identify the original jump set.

items.title: A Construction of Cauchy Data for Trapped Surface Formation in the Massive Einstein--Klein--Gordon System
items.summary: We construct a class of smooth, spherically symmetric, asymptotically flat Cauchy data for the massive Einstein--Klein--Gordon system that are initially untrapped but give rise to trapped surface formation in their maximal Cauchy developments. These data coincide with contracting Friedmann--Lemaître--Robertson--Walker (FLRW) data on an interior ball and with Schwarzschild data outside a larger ball. The data can also be made to have arbitrarily small compactness: the ratio $2m/r$, where $m$ is the Hawking mass and $r$ is the area radius, can be made arbitrarily small throughout the initial Cauchy hypersurface.

items.title: Class number of real quadratic fields of explicit discriminant
items.summary: In this paper, we study the class numbers of a family of real quadratic fields $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{D})$ whose discriminants possess a specific exponential structure. More precisely, the discriminant $D$ is given by $(b(4bs+1)^k+s)^2 + (4bs+1)^k$, where $b$, $s$ and $k$ are positive integers, and $D$ is assumed to be square-free. This non-Richaud-Degert family is characterized by a predictable continued fraction expansion for $\sqrt{D}$, which allows for an explicit expression of its fundamental unit. When the parameters $b$ and $s$ are fixed, the corresponding regulators grow asymptotically like $(\log D)^2$. By analyzing the associated partial twisted zeta functions at $z=0$ and applying algebraic methods inspired by the strategies of Biró, we derive explicit criteria under which the class number $h(D)$ is strictly greater than $1$. Our work contributes to the long-standing mathematical tradition that aims to solve the "class number one problem" for explicit families of real quadratic fields.

items.title: Rectifiable measures in Ahlfors regular spaces: endpoint constructions
items.summary: A theorem of Balka and Keleti implies that on any complete separable metric space $\mathbb{X}$, every locally finite Borel measure $μ$ of packing dimension strictly less than $m$ is "Euclidean-like" insofar as there exist Lipschitz maps $f_i:E_i\subset\mathbb{R}^m\rightarrow\mathbb{X}$ such that $μ(\mathbb{X}\setminus\bigcup_1^\infty f_i(E_i))=0$. An ongoing challenge in geometric measure theory is to understand when this property, called $m$-rectifiability, holds for measures of packing dimension $m$. Towards this goal, we prove that every complete Ahlfors $q$-regular metric space with $q\geq m$ supports $m$-rectifiable doubling measures of packing dimension $m$. The proof of existence of such measures is new even when $\mathbb{X}=\mathbb{R}^n$ and $n>m$. More generally, on every complete Ahlfors $q$-regular metric space with $q>m-1$, we construct $m$-rectifiable, purely $(m-1)$-unrectifiable measures with any prescribed exact Hausdorff and packing dimensions $0\leq s_H\leq s_P\leq q$ with $m-1\leq s_P\leq m$, which are doubling when $s_H>0$. This verifies a conjecture of Badger and Schul. The design of the measures relies on metric cubes with variable scaling, in which the ratio of consecutive side lengths tends to infinity but jumps only on a sparse set of generations, together with Badger and Schul's square packing construction of Lipschitz maps.

items.title: Examples of homological mirror symmetry via Zariski descent
items.summary: This paper considers a general setting in which the Fukaya category of an exact symplectic manifold may be decomposed as a fiber product of Fukaya categories of smaller pieces. We establish a property of Fukaya categories that is mirror to Zariski descent of coherent sheaves. This fits into a natural strategy to prove homological mirror symmetry by a local-to-global analysis. The examples we consider in detail are open Riemann surfaces and exact log Calabi-Yau surfaces, and we provide proofs of homological mirror symmetry in these cases.

items.title: Noetherian connected braided Hopf algebras are affine
items.summary: The well-known Wu--Zhang question asks whether every Noetherian Hopf algebra over a field is affine (finitely generated as an algebra). In this paper, we extend this fundamental problem to the braided setting within the monoidal category ${}_{H}^{H}\mathcal{YD}$ of left Yetter--Drinfel'd modules over a Hopf algebra $H$. By developing term-rewriting methods based on reduction orderings and prime-word factorizations in free prebraided algebras, we establish explicit expansions for YD-triangular comultiplications. We prove that if $(\mathbb{K}\langle X \rangle, ε)$ is an augmented free algebra in ${}_{H}^{H}\mathcal{YD}$ and $I \subseteq \ker ε$ is an ideal invariant under a YD-triangular comultiplication, then every $I$-reducible letter---and consequently every non-empty word in $\langle X \rangle$---can be expressed modulo $I$ as a linear combination of products of $I$-irreducible letters strictly smaller with respect to the reduction order. As a primary consequence, we prove that any right Noetherian connected prebraided Hopf algebra $B$ in ${}_{H}^{H}\mathcal{YD}$ is affine, generated by the image of a finite set $X_{I}$ of $I$-irreducible letters. As an application, we show that the braided component $B = A^{\mathrm{co}\,π}$ of a right Noetherian Radford biproduct $A = B \sharp H$ is affine whenever $A_{(0)} \subseteq \jmath(H)$, reducing the affineness of $A$ entirely to that of $H$.

items.title: Whittaker supermodules for the Takiff superalgebra \mathfrak{osp}(1|2)
items.summary: In this article, we classify all simple Whittaker supermodules over the Takiff Lie superalgebra \(\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)\otimes\mathbb C[t]/(t^2)\), associated with Whittaker characters defined on the even part of its positive nilpotent subalgebra.

items.title: Anosov representations from cyclic Higgs bundles
items.summary: For every complex simple Lie group G (not of type $E_8$) we construct the minimal Slodowy slice, which is a half-dimensional slice in the character variety of a closed surface group into G, containing the composition of Fuchsian representations with the minimal representation of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ in G and invariant under the mapping class group action. This slice is defined via cyclic Higgs bundles, and we show that when G is not of type $E_8$, the corresponding representations are Anosov, so in particular discrete and faithful, and dominate some Fuchsian representation. For each of these Higgs bundles, we consider the equivariant harmonic map to the symmetric space, and we show it is an embedding and a quasi-isometric embedding with regard to the induced metric. From the cyclicity of these Higgs bundles we are also able to construct an auxiliary harmonic map to a pseudoriemannian symmetric space $G/G^σ$ which is also an embedding. Our techniques also apply to harmonic Higgs bundles over the unit disk satisfying a certain completeness condition. These techniques also apply to two other families of cyclic Higgs bundles.

items.title: Negative-Dimensional Simplicial Complexes via the Grothendieck Group of the Join Monoid
items.summary: We introduce a framework that extends classical combinatorial and topological notions of simplicial complexes to a setting that includes simplicial complexes of negative dimension. This is achieved by considering the Grothendieck group of the commutative monoid of finite simplicial complexes under the join operation, which provides formal inverses and allows negative-dimensional objects to be defined. Within this group we adapt standard invariants such as $f$- and $h$-vectors, their corresponding polynomials, and the Euler characteristic. The same construction naturally endows the Grothendieck group with an Alexandroff topology. We show that this space is universal for finite topological spaces, and consequently the associated ordered simplicial complex is universal within its class.

items.title: Flagged Grothendieck enumerators and ribbon decomposition determinants
items.summary: We establish Hamel--Goulden-type ribbon decomposition determinantal formulas for a new class of symmetric functions called flagged Grothendieck enumerators. In particular, these functions generalize both canonical refined stable Grothendieck polynomials and their duals. The proof uses Talaska's formula via flows on planar lattice graphs with systems of paths and cycles.

items.title: Composite local observables of sine-Gordon via stochastic analysis
items.summary: We develop a rigorous framework for the description of general local composite observables in Euclidean quantum field theories. The approach is nonperturbative and combines renormalisation group ideas with techniques of stochastic analysis. Via renormalisation dictated by sufficiently precise approximate solution theory of corresponding flow equations, we construct various local observables of the sine-Gordon model on the full space up to $β^2<6π$, including highly singular ones such as vertex fields $\exp(iαφ(y))$ in the optimal Wick regime $|\operatorname{Re}(α)|<4π/β$ and derivatives of arbitrarily high order, i.e. $\partial^μφ(y)$ for any multiindex $μ\in \mathbb{N}^2_0$. Applications of the approach include a direct proof of smoothness of observable-inserted correlation functions, and verification that the constructed objects satisfy a version of the prefactorization algebra axioms adapted to our setting.

items.title: Joint universality of the Riemann zeta-function with arbitrary real shift parameters
items.summary: We prove joint universality of the Riemann zeta-function for shifts $ζ(s+id_jτ)$ with arbitrary nonzero real parameters $d_j$ whose absolute values are pairwise distinct, and show that these conditions are optimal. As a consequence, we establish generalized strong recurrence for every finite family of nonzero real parameters, meaning that the corresponding shifts of the Riemann zeta-function simultaneously approximate each other. The only cases for which generalized strong recurrence remains unproved are those involving both zero and nonzero shift parameters, for which it is equivalent to the Riemann hypothesis. Our proof combines Emsalem's generalization of the six exponentials theorem with a generalization of Pecherskii's rearrangement theorem that may be of independent interest.

items.title: Irrationality and Noether--Lefschetz loci in the moduli space of K3 surfaces
items.summary: The goal of this paper is twofold. First, we construct examples of families of surfaces where the locus of points in the base with constant degree of irrationality is not constructible. Second, we explore the notion of gonality loci in the moduli space of K3 surfaces, which are characterized by the existence of a smooth curve with fixed gonality. Among various results, we prove that polarized gonality loci are always unions of Noether--Lefschetz divisors.

items.title: Subperiodic groups and bounded automorphisms of periodic graphs
items.summary: A subperiodic group is a group of motions of $d$-dimensional Euclidean space $\mathbb R^d$ which contains a translation lattice $\mathbb Z^r$ of rank $r < d$ as a subgroup of finite index. Cayley graphs of subperiodic groups are used to illustrate the concept of bounded automorphisms (particularly of finite order), i.e. those when the distance between a graph vertex and its image has an upper bound. The description of subperiodic groups in dimension 3 in terms of subgroup structure and abstract group isomorphism types [75 crystallographic rod groups ($r=1$) and 80 layer groups ($r=2$) belong to 32 and 34 types, respectively] allows for a convenient characterization of bounded automorphisms of their Cayley graphs. An easy-to-compute set of invariants is developed for recognizing the isomorphism types of crystallographic groups in $\mathbb R^3$ from finite presentations which makes use of only the number of nonconjugate subgroups up to a given finite index $n$ ($n \leq 12$ for rod groups, $n \leq 8$ for layer groups, and $n \leq 24$ for space groups), and how many of them are normal. A criterion is proven that if a finite (inverse-closed) generating set of a group $G$ is stabilized by conjugation by a nontrivial element of finite order in $G$, then the respective Cayley graph possesses nontrivial bounded automorphisms of finite order. This criterion is applied to three-periodic sphere-packing graphs. Subperiodic groups in $\mathbb R^4$ with a three-dimensional translation lattice are used to systematically derive embeddings of three-periodic ladder graphs in $\mathbb R^3$.

items.title: Intermediate Growth and Rigidity in Primitive Circulant Spectral Algebras
items.summary: At prime graph orders, the complete nontrivial and primitive Fourier spectra of a circulant coincide. We show that this agreement conceals a strong algebraic separation when the graph order varies. For any nonempty finite jump set $S$, let $A_S^{\mathrm{prim}}$ be the algebra of arithmetic functions obtained by evaluating symmetric power sums on the primitive spectrum, filtered by power-sum weight. Removing the common Euler-totient term gives a reduced, locally finite algebra $B_S$, and we prove a filtration-preserving isomorphism $A_S^{\mathrm{prim}}\cong B_S[T_2]$. Thus $A_S^{\mathrm{prim}}$ is non-Noetherian and has Krull dimension one. Its filtered dimensions satisfy $\exp(c_S\sqrt{D/\log D})\leq ρ_S^{\mathrm{prim}}(D) \leq\exp(C_S\sqrt D)$ for large $D$, and its associated-graded Hilbert series is nonrational. Despite agreement on every prime order, the primitive and full spectral evaluation algebras intersect only in $\mathbb{Q}$. More strongly, no nonconstant primitive spectral function is eventually quasirational on residue classes. We give an exact finite-matrix rank formula and determine the quotient obtained by restricting to integers with large prime factors.

items.title: Virtual Two-Step Nilpotency of the Fundamental Groups of Special Quasi-Projective Varieties
items.summary: We prove that the fundamental group of every smooth connected complex quasi-projective variety that is special in the sense of Campana is virtually nilpotent of class at most two. This establishes the two-step nilpotency conjecture of Cao--Deng--Hacon--Păun, a quasi-projective analogue of Campana's almost abelian conjecture for special compact Kähler manifolds. Examples of Cadorel--Deng--Yamanoi show that the step bound is sharp. On a suitable finite etale cover, we construct a canonical second Albanese map to a torus torsor over an abelian variety. The proof reduces to showing that the kernel of the induced map on fundamental groups is finite. Using good minimal models and meridian groups of projective pairs, we show that an infinite kernel would yield a saturated rank-one subsheaf of logarithmic differentials whose Iitaka dimension contradicts specialness.

items.title: Policy Optimization in the Linear Quadratic Gaussian Problem: A Frequency Domain Perspective
items.summary: The Linear Quadratic Gaussian (LQG) problem is a classic and widely studied model in optimal control, providing a fundamental framework for designing controllers for linear systems subject to process and observation noises. In recent years, researchers have increasingly focused on directly parameterizing dynamic controllers and optimizing the LQG cost over the resulting parameterized set. However, this parameterization typically gives rise to a highly non-convex optimization landscape for the resulting parameterized LQG problem. To our knowledge, there is currently no general method for certifying the global optimality of candidate controller parameters in this setting. In this work, we address these gaps with the following contributions. First, we derive a necessary and sufficient condition for the global optimality of stationary points in a parameterized LQG problem. This condition reduces the verification of optimality to a test of the controllability and observability for a novel, specially constructed transfer function, yielding a precise and computationally tractable certificate. Furthermore, our condition provides a rigorous explanation for why traditional parameterizations can lead to suboptimal stationary points. Second, we elevate the controller parameter space from conventional finite-dimensional settings to the infinite-dimensional $\mathcal{RH}_\infty$ space and develop a gradient-based algorithm in this setting, for which we provide a theoretical analysis establishing global convergence. Finally, representative numerical experiments validate the theoretical findings and demonstrate the practical viability of the proposed approach. Additionally, the appendix section explores a data-driven extension to the model-free setting, where we outline a parameter estimation scheme and demonstrate its practical viability through numerical simulation.

items.title: Low-rank cross approximation of function-valued tensors for reduced-order modeling of parametric PDEs
items.summary: The paper considers function-valued tensors, viewed as multidimensional arrays with entries in an abstract Hilbert space. Despite the absence of the algebraic structure of a field, the geometric inner-product structure suffices to introduce the Tucker rank, higher-order SVD, and Tucker-cross decomposition for function-valued tensors. An adaptive cross-approximation algorithm is developed to compute low-rank approximations of such tensors. The framework is motivated by, and applied to, model order reduction of the parameter-to-solution map for a parametric PDE. The resulting reduced-order model can be interpreted as an encoder-decoder scheme with a nonlinear encoder and a multilinear decoder. The performance of the proposed non-intrusive approximation method is demonstrated in numerical examples for two nonlinear parametric PDE systems.

items.title: From Worst-Case to Smoothed Complexity in Continuous Optimization
items.summary: Worst-case complexity bounds often fail to reflect the practical performance of optimization algorithms, while average-case complexity heavily relies on the distribution of the input. In this work, we develop a smoothed-analysis framework for classical continuous optimization algorithms by studying their behaviour on random perturbations of arbitrary functions. Our main contribution is to apply methods suited for non-degenerate functions to perturbations of degenerate functions, thereby recovering the faster best-known rates for the non-degenerate class. We derive smoothed complexity guarantees for several standard methods, including (Accelerated) Gradient Descent, Conjugate Gradient, and Newton-type methods, under various settings including nonconvex ones, and show that these bounds can substantially improve upon their worst-case guarantees, bringing them closer to the practical behaviour of the respective methods.

items.title: Feedback Stabilization for Sampled Linear Systems with Control-linear Noise
items.summary: In this paper, we consider linear stochastic systems with control-linear noise and periodically sampled measurements. We address the problem of feedback stabilization in the mean-square sense. The main contribution of the paper is to provide a necessary and sufficient condition for feedback stabilization. In particular, we relate feedback stabilizability of the stochastic system to the existence of a fixed point of a Riccati-type algebraic equation and, further, to the existence of a solution to an infinite-horizon optimal control problem.

items.title: The Bruce-Roberts Tjurina number of holomorphic 1-forms along complex analytic varieties
items.summary: We introduce the notion of the \textit{Bruce-Roberts Tjurina number} for holomorphic 1-forms with respect to a pair $(X,V)$ of complex analytic subvarieties. We characterize its finiteness and, when $X$ and $V$ are hypersurfaces with at most isolated singularities, relate it to a determinantal colength, the Tjurina number of the 1-form with respect to $V$, and the Tjurina number of $X$. We also establish a decomposition of the difference between the Bruce-Roberts Milnor and Tjurina numbers and a bound for their quotient. As an application, we prove a relative quasihomogeneity result for germs of non-dicritical generalized curve foliations in complex dimension two.

items.title: Thales's theorem in higher dimensions
items.summary: In the Euclidean plane, Thales's theorem is equivalent to the statement that a quadrilateral with two opposite right angles has a circumscribed circle. We generalize the latter to higher dimensions: a convex polytope with two distinguished vertices, the \emph{poles}, such that the faces spanned by the two poles are perpendicular, is inscribed in the sphere whose diameter joins its poles. These \emph{orthogonally bipolar} polytopes are exactly the bipolar polytopes of a companion paper that arise as cutouts by orthogonal projections. As an application we show that for a polytope $P$ and a point $B$, the balls with diameters $[V,B]$, $V$ a vertex of $P$, cover $P$, and that the power diagram of their boundary spheres refines this covering to a tiling.
