For integer cubes $[-R,R]^d \cap \mathbb{Z}^d$ and the sign cube $\{-1,1\}^d$, totally unimodular encodings improve on the upper bounds from direct circuit decomposition, while random perturbations of Hadamard matrices give new lower bounds. A key ingredient is a uniform affine Bernoulli variant of Nguyen and Wood's surjectivity theorem. In every sufficiently large dimension the sign-cube lower bound is $d^{d/2}2^{-d-o(d)}$, and the integer-cube lower bound is $R^d d^{d/2}2^{-o(d)}$ uniformly for polynomially bounded integer radii. For random sign-cube sequences of even length conditioned on summing to zero, we prove a sharp threshold from irreducibility to reducibility at $d\log d/\log 4$, far below the extremal scale. For fixed $p$ and $R$, we determine exact exponential rates for lattice $\ell_p$-balls when $p=1$, $R\geq3$, or $2\leq p<\infty$, $\lfloor R^p\rfloor\geq3$. For each fixed integer $k\geq3$, we determine the exponential rate of the worst-case $\ell_1$-distance from an optimal LP vertex to the nearest integer optimum in standard-form programs with ternary matrices having at most $k$ nonzero entries per column.

items.title: A new notion of Dirichlet boundary condition for elliptic equation of divergence form
items.summary: In this paper, we consider Dirichlet boundary conditions for elliptic equations in divergence form on rough domains by introducing a truncation-based weak solution framework that circumvents global Sobolev trace obstacles. We establish well-posedness on bounded admissible domains for continuous boundary data and $L^2$ sources, deriving boundary Hölder regularities that require only uniform ellipticity and an exterior measure-density condition. This approach eliminates the uniform domain regularity and coefficient continuity imnposed in Guam, Wang and Zhou(2026). Furthermore, on sufficiently flat Reifenberg domains, we obtain boundary $C^α$ regularity for any $α\in (0,1) $ using natural energy estimates, thereby bypassing $L^p$($p>\frac {n}{2}$) restrictions found in Lian and Zhang(2026). Crucially, we obtain global $H^1$ regularity for Hölder boundary data ($α>\frac 12$) a posteriori, without requiring small-BMO coefficient assumptions on the coefficients.

items.title: Integrability of the horizontal mean curvature near characteristic points in the Heisenberg group
items.summary: We investigate the local integrability of the horizontal mean curvature near characteristic points of surfaces in the first Heisenberg group. We prove that, for every embedded surface of class $C^{2,α}$, with $α>0$, the horizontal mean curvature is locally integrable with respect to (any) Riemannian surface measure, without any assumption on the structure of the characteristic set. We further establish that the horizontal unit normal belongs to $BV_{\mathrm{loc}}$ and characterize its $W^{1,1}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ regularity in terms of the vanishing one-dimensional Hausdorff measure of the characteristic set. Finally, we answer an open question by Danielli, Garofalo and Nhieu by constructing a $C^2$ surface with a unique characteristic point whose horizontal mean curvature fails to be locally integrable, thus showing that the additional Hölder regularity cannot, in general, be replaced by $C^2$ regularity.

items.title: L^p-boundedness of the Bochner-Riesz operator
items.summary: In this paper, we give a new approach to the Bochner-Riesz summability. As a result, we show that the Bochner-Riesz operator $\mathbf{S}^δ, 0<\Reδ<{1\over 2}$ is bounded on $\mathbf{L}^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ for ${n-1\over 2n}\leq {1\over p}\leq{n+1\over 2n}$.

items.title: Mesoscopic derivation of predator-prey dynamics via diffusive fast-reaction asymptotics: cross-diffusion and fear effects
items.summary: We propose a kinetic derivation of a spatial predator-prey model with cross-diffusion interactions and a Beddington-DeAngelis functional response. At the mesoscopic level, we divide the two populations into distinct behavioral states: prey can be active or hidden in a refuge, while predators can be either searching or handling. The microscopic state of each subpopulation is described in terms of group size and a continuous directional velocity variable, with state transitions governed by suitable Boltzmann-type interaction operators. By combining a diffusive scaling with a slow-fast formulation of the kinetic reaction operators, we formally derive a macroscopic reaction-cross-diffusion system for the total population densities of prey and predators. The limiting model consistently recovers the Beddington-DeAngelis functional response along with its associated nonlinear diffusion terms. Crucially, the kinetic upscaling yields a predator-dependent prey growth term taking a logistic form with an effective carrying capacity. This carrying capacity depends non-monotonically on predator density because prey redistribute between active and refuge states. Since density-dependent competition acts separately within these behavioral states, intermediate predator levels reduce aggregate crowding and thereby increase the effective carrying capacity of the total prey population. Overall, our derivation provides a mechanistic link connecting predator-induced behavioral shifts, refuge use, and macroscopic cross-diffusion.

items.title: Euclidean Ramsey Theory for Lines and Finite Configurations
items.summary: A classical question in Euclidean Ramsey theory, posed by Erdős, Graham, Montgomery, Rothschild, Spencer, and Straus, asks which finite configurations $X\subset\mathbb E^2$ must appear in blue under every red--blue coloring of the plane having no red pair of points distance one apart. For $m \ge 2$, let $\ell_m$ denote the line of $m$ points with consecutive points distance one apart. Tsaturian showed that $\ell_5$ is unavoidable; we improve this to $\ell_7$. Additionally, we show that in every three-coloring of the plane in which two colors contain no $\ell_2$, the third color must contain an $\ell_3$. To conclude our discussion on lines, we prove several related results on two-colorings of higher-dimensional Euclidean spaces where both colors avoid longer lines. Our methods also extend to other point configurations. In any two-coloring of the plane in which one color contains no $\ell_2$, we show that the other color must contain both a regular pentagon of side length one and a unit square together with its center. We also prove that every two-coloring of three-dimensional space contains either a monochromatic unit square or a monochromatic noncoplanar tetrahedron with four edges of length one and two of length $\sqrt{2}$. Our proofs combine Székely's averaging inequalities for distance-avoiding sets with the Fourier-analytic and linear-programming methods of de Oliveira Filho and Vallentin, together with a theorem on rotation-invariant measures from OpenAI's recent work on the Hadwiger-Nelson problem.

items.title: Sharp asymptotic stability of the incompressible porous medium equation on the whole plane
items.summary: We study the asymptotic stability of the steady state $e_s(x)=-x_2$ of the incompressible porous media equation in $\mathbb R^2$. For every $s>2$, we prove that sufficiently small initial perturbations $θ_0\in H^s(\mathbb R^2)$ of $e_s$ generate unique global solutions $ρ=e_s+θ$, where $θ$ remains uniformly bounded in $H^s$ and converges strongly to zero in $H^s$ as $t\to\infty$. The main innovations of this work are threefold. First, exploiting the structure of the equation, we construct a weighted energy that eliminates the need to control $\|\nabla u^2\|_{L^1_tL^\infty_x}$. Second, rather than estimating the anisotropic commutators directly, we study the integral terms containing these commutators and establish suitable bounds through refined computations in frequency space. Third, we establish convergence in the highest-order $H^s$ norm under uniform energy bounds involving only an $L^\infty_tH^s_x$ bound on $θ$ and an $L^2_tH^s_x$ bound on $\mathcal R_1θ$.

items.title: On compact subsets of the plane
items.summary: We construct a family F of compact and pathwise connected subsets of the Euclidean plane such that (i) the cardinality of F is that of the continuum (and hence extremely large) and (ii) if X,Y are distinct spaces in F then there never exists a topological embedding from X into Y.

items.title: Adaptive Reparametrized Time for Score-Based Diffusion Sampling
items.summary: We study timestep allocation for score-based diffusion sampling, where a learned reverse-time dynamics is discretized on a finite grid. Uniform and hand-crafted schedules are standard choices, but they rely on fixed prescriptions and can therefore be suboptimal. To address this limitation, we propose Adaptive Reparameterized Time (ART), a continuous-time control formulation that learns a time change by treating the speed of the sampling clock as the control, so that a uniform grid on the learned clock induces adaptive timesteps in the original diffusion time. Based on a leading-order Euler error surrogate, ART provides a principled objective for allocating timesteps along the sampling trajectory. To solve this deterministic control problem, we introduce ART-RL, an auxiliary randomized formulation with Gaussian policies that turns schedule learning into a continuous-time reinforcement learning problem. We prove that the randomized ART-RL formulation is equivalent to ART at the optimizer level, in the sense that its optimal Gaussian policy recovers the optimal ART time-warping rate through its mean. We further establish policy evaluation and policy improvement characterizations and derive trajectory-based moment identities that yield implementable actor--critic updates for learning the schedule. Across experiments ranging from controlled low-dimensional settings to image generation, ART-RL can be plugged into existing diffusion samplers by changing only the timestep grid, consistently improving sample quality over strong baseline schedules at matched budgets while leaving the rest of the sampling pipeline unchanged. The learned schedules also exhibit broad generalization, transferring without retraining across sampling budgets, datasets, solvers, pipelines, and representation spaces.

items.title: Fujita's Very Ampleness Conjecture for $\mathbb{P}^{n-1}$-Bundles over Curves
items.summary: Let $\mathcal{E}$ be a vector bundle of rank $n\geq 2$ over a smooth projective curve $C$ over $\mathbb{C}$. We prove that $ω_{\mathbb{P}_C(\mathcal{E})}\otimes\mathcal{L}_1\otimes\dots\otimes\mathcal{L}_k$ is very ample for arbitrary ample line bundles $\mathcal{L}_i$ on ${\mathbb{P}_C(\mathcal{E})}$ when $k\geq n+2$.

items.title: Adding unbounded and not bounded sets to a singular cardinal
items.summary: This paper solves a problem (SP) attributed to Solovay in the 1960s, which is to add an unbounded sequence to a singular cardinal $κ$ without adding bounded subsets to $κ$, while preserving $κ^+$. The solution applies to any cofinality of the singular cardinal, with the assumption that $κ$ is a strong limit needed for the case of uncountable cofinality. Unsuccessful attempts to solve (SP), mostly for the countable cofinality, have appeared in published papers by various authors.

items.title: Non-closed products in branch and weakly branch groups
items.summary: We prove that the first Grigorchuk group and the Gupta-Sidki $3$-group are not double coset separable, disproving a conjecture of Grigorchuk, Leemann and Nagnibeda. More generally, every finitely generated regular branch group with bounded activity contains two finitely generated, profinitely closed subgroups with trivial intersection whose product is not closed. Every infinite finitely generated subgroup of the first Grigorchuk group or the Gupta-Sidki $3$-group also fails to be double coset separable. We extend the construction to the $p$-Basilica groups and, using polynomial activity, to the long-range group, whose derived subgroup we prove to be finitely generated. Under an additional hypothesis on finite quotients, we determine the closure of the product. Membership in the constructed product is decidable in the first Grigorchuk group.

items.title: Asymptotically good codes from Siegel modular varieties
items.summary: We construct asymptotically good codes by evaluating Siegel modular forms at superspecial points on congruence towers of Siegel modular varieties. For every genus $g\ge2$ and every fixed weight $w\ge g+1$, the construction gives such a family in sufficiently large characteristic, over a finite field which is independent of the level of the tower. The towers can be chosen so that this field is $\mathbb{F}_{p^2}$. We give an explicit lower bound for the asymptotic rate. The lower bound for the relative minimum distance follows from the Pieri formula on the space of flags in the Hodge bundle and an intersection argument along its strata. We also prove that, for $p\ge5$ and $0\le w\le p+1$, the kernel of evaluation in every genus consists precisely of the multiples of the ordinary Hasse invariant. For $g=2,3$, the geometry of the supersingular locus gives explicit bounds for the relative minimum distance and recovery sets whose sizes are bounded independently of the level.

items.title: Plancherel Identities for unbounded subsets of $\mathbb R^d$
items.summary: We investigate spectral pairs associated with unbounded subsets of $\mathbb R^d$ that are periodic with respect to full-rank lattices. We establish a characterization of such spectral pairs in terms of the spectrality of an associated bounded fundamental component. More precisely, we prove that the Fourier transform defines an isometric isomorphism onto an $L^2$ space with an explicitly determined absolutely continuous pair measure, supported on a union of translates of a dual-lattice fundamental domain, if and only if the bounded component admits an orthogonal basis of exponential functions with frequencies in the dual lattice. In particular, the Plancherel identity alone is sufficient to characterize these spectral pairs. As an application, when the bounded component tiles $\br^d$ by a lattice, we obtain an equivalence between certain translational tiling properties of unbounded periodic sets and the existence of the corresponding Plancherel identities. We also examine periodicity properties of sets that tile by finite translation sets, highlighting distinctions between the one-dimensional and higher-dimensional settings.

items.title: A generalized Vojta-Rémond inequality over adelic curves
items.summary: We extend Dill's generalized Vojta-Rémond inequality to proper adelic curves of characteristic zero, under an explicit Siegel hypothesis. The geometric case is closely related to recent work on Mordell-Lang plus geometric Bogomolov for semi-abelian varieties. Our formulation retains Dill's generality for products of distinct projective varieties. The appendix establishes the Siegel input for arithmetic function fields with nef and big polarizations on the model.

items.title: Construction, Enumeration and Duality of Perfectly Balanced Musical Sets of Order $2pq$
items.summary: In this paper, we present a comprehensive study of perfectly balanced musical sets, also known in the literature as vanishing sums of roots of unity, in the particular case of order $2pq$. Starting from the well-established result concerning the decomposition of such sets as an integer linear combination of regular polygons, we first provide an algebraic formalization that allows to explicitly construct all these sets. We then propose six different decompositions of each set into regular polygons. Moreover, by investigating their combinatorial enumeration, we derive a formula for the exact number of these sets for a given order $2pq$, and describe their distribution and cardinality for the particular case of order $6p$. One of the main results concerns the duality that can be established between these sets. In particular, we prove that every non-periodic minimal perfectly balanced set of order $2pq$ can be combined with another one to produce a self-complementary $2p$-periodic set, and the reciprocal also holds. Finally, we demonstrate that the modulus of the discrete Fourier transform coefficients of dual sets are related. All these results shed new light on the distribution of perfectly balanced sets of order $2pq$ and suggest new mathematical questions in a more general case.

items.title: Fitting Gaussian vectors in normed spaces
items.summary: Given a family of $N$ i.i.d. Gaussian points in a $d$-dimensional normed space, what is the probability that some linear transformation maps it to the unit sphere? The case of a Euclidean space is known as the ellipsoid fitting problem and has recently attracted major attention. We initiate a study of this fitting problem in a general normed space, both asymptotically and in a fixed dimension. We specifically focus on the space $\ell_\infty^d$, where a combinatorial reformulation allows us to show that $cd^2/\log d$ points can be fitted with high probability. We illustrate that the geometry of the normed space is reflected in the fitting problem by showing that in dimension $2$, the spaces $\ell_2^2$ and $\ell_\infty^2$ are characterized by having extremal fittability properties. We also study the probability that a family of $N$ i.i.d.\ Gaussian points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ is in convex position and show that a sharp threshold occurs around the value $N=\exp(d/2e)$.

items.title: Loops and mirrors
items.summary: For a smooth affine complex variety X we construct a Q-algebra LH(X), loop cohomology, in terms of the formal-loop space of X. We conjecture that it is isomorphic to the symplectic cohomology of X. The degree-zero loop cohomology subalgebra is finitely generated for polarized log Calabi-Yau X, constructing an intrinsic mirror affine coordinate ring. Its polyvector algebra is identified with the full loop cohomology algebra for a positive log Calabi-Yau pair with maximal boundary and smooth loop mirror, proving a form of mirror symmetry. In this case we further identify the degree-zero loop cohomology algebra with the Gross-Siebert intrinsic mirror algebra. Assuming in addition that X is a surface, we prove that the full loop and symplectic cohomology algebras agree.

items.title: Thom Morphisms, Self-Intersection, and the Sectional Category of a Section
items.summary: For sections between simply connected spaces of finite rational type, we compare module sectional category, sectional category and relative category after rationalization. Fibre Poincaré duality turns the compatibility of derived evaluation with the section into a derived self-intersection formula. We prove equality of the three invariants under any of four hypotheses: a base-dimension bound, finite total rational homotopy of the fibre, a smooth section with closed manifold fibre, or a compatible relative Frobenius model. Projective bundles over CP^k with fibre CP^r have common value k + r, which is unbounded even for fixed fibre. Whether fibre Poincaré duality alone suffices remains open.

items.title: Logarithmic gradient estimate and Universal bounds for semilinear elliptic equations revisited
items.summary: We derive the complete and optimal Cheng--Yau gradient estimates and universal bounds for subcritical semilinear elliptic equations on Riemannian manifolds with (Bakry-Émery) Ricci curvature bounded below. This answers a fundamental question that has existed for a long time. As a corollary, this provides a new proof of the Gidas-Spruck classical Liouville theorem. The Harnack inequality is also obtained.

items.title: Numerical investigation of a MST conjecture for random Haar matrices
items.summary: The state-to-state control time of finite-dimensional conservative bilinear quantum systems is bounded by the weight of minimum spanning trees (MST) derived from the drift matrices. For a spectrum scaling as k^3/2 , determining whether the control time vanishes as the dimension d tends to infinity remains an open problem due to the global correlations imposed by the Haar measure. We formulate two conjectures regarding the asymptotic behavior of the MST weight\,: a general decay to zero, and a scaling in 1/sqrt(ln d) derived from an independent Gaussian surrogate model. Numerical investigations up to dimension d = 18101 validate the general decay, confirm that the exact Haar model and the independent surrogate are statistically indistinguishable in mean at all tested dimensions, and extract the thermodynamic limit $α$ = 10/3, which both models approach from below once the scaling variable 1/ ln d is adopted.

items.title: Equivariant Quantisation of Hypertoric Varieties via Symplectic Cuts
items.summary: We study the equivariant geometric quantisation of a non-compact hypertoric orbifold of complex dimension $2n$ by compact symplectic cuts. When the defining arrangement has a non-empty bounded base region and the fixed lift is integral, we prove that, at every positive regular integral level $d$, the space of sections on the cut is the sum of the fibre-rotation weight spaces of weight at most $d$ in the original quantisation. The higher cohomology of the cut pre-quantum line orbibundle vanishes, so its equivariant index is the character of its actual section space. Using the moment polyptychs introduced in a companion paper, we give an orbifold Kawasaki-Riemann-Roch localisation formula for this character. We also compute it as a weighted lattice-point sum: a residual weight $x$ occurs at level $d$ if and only if the arrangement slack function satisfies $\mathcal{S}(x) \leq d$, with multiplicity $\binom{d - \mathcal{S}(x) + n}{n}$. The examples compare these calculations in rank one, including a cut with an orbifold point, and in rank two, for smooth cuts that are not toric.

items.title: Discrete-Time Stochastic Control Beyond i.i.d. Noise
items.summary: We study discrete-time stochastic control problems where the noise driving the state dynamics is a stationary infinite-order chain rather than an i.i.d. sequence. We formulate the problem as a controlled Markov process by enlarging the state space to include the posterior distribution of the noise given the state-action history. Assuming that the sensitivity of the noise transition kernel to past noise values decays exponentially, we show that the expected total variation distance between the full-history and finite-memory noise filters decays at rate $\sqrt{N}ρ^{\sqrt{N}}$. We use this result to construct finite-memory control models and establish explicit near-optimality bounds for their policies. Finally, under suitable ergodicity conditions, we show that Q-learning converges to the optimal solution of the approximate model, so the same performance bounds apply to the learned policies.

items.title: Invariant measures, Gelfand pairs and integral representations
items.summary: We prove that whenever a Gelfand pair acts cocompactly on a locally compact space, there is a measure relatively invariant under a "parabolic" subgroup. That result seems new even for simple Lie groups, in which case it admits a much more direct proof. Along the way, we obtain for general Gelfand pairs a variant of Furstenberg's invariant ray theorem for minimal parabolics. We use this to establish an integral representation theorem for positive spherical functions in complete generality, extending the Harish-Chandra representation. A similar representation theorem is given for positive harmonic functions.

items.title: A New insight into the Ambrosio--Reshetnyak approach to Sobolev maps
items.summary: Given $p \in (1,\infty)$, let $\operatorname{X}=(\operatorname{X},ρ,μ)$ be a metric measure space such that $(\operatorname{X},\operatorname{d})$ is complete, the measure $μ$ is uniformly locally doubling and $\operatorname{X}$ supports a weak local $(1,p)$-Poincaré inequality. Let $(\operatorname{Y},\operatorname{d},\underline{y})$ be a complete pointed metric space. We prove that the equivalence class (modulo coincidence $μ$-a.e.) of a Borel map $u:\operatorname{X} \to \operatorname{Y}$ with a separable range belongs to the Ambrosio--Reshetnyak--Sobolev class $W_{p}^{1}(\operatorname{X},\operatorname{Y})$ if and only if $h \circ u$ belongs to the Sobolev space $W_{p}^{1}(\operatorname{X})$ for every $1$-Lipschitz function $h:\operatorname{Y} \to \mathbb{R}$ with $h(\underline{y})=0$.

items.title: Representations of the quantum double of the restricted quantum group $\mathbf{\overline{u}}_q(\mathfrak{sl_2})$
items.summary: Let $q$ be a primitive $2p$-th root of unity with $p\ge2$, and let $H=D(\mathbf{\overline{u}}_q(\mathfrak{sl_2}))$ be the Drinfeld double of the restricted quantum group $\mathbf{\overline{u}}_q(\mathfrak{sl_2})$. We describe the dual Hopf algebra and the cross relations of $H$. A change of generator gives a classification of the simple $H$-modules. Their isomorphism classes are indexed by $\mathbb Z_{2p}^{\,2}$. We construct their projective covers, compute their dimensions, and determine which simple modules are projective. Finally, we prove that $H$ is strictly wild for every $p\ge2$ by constructing a fully faithful exact functor from finite-dimensional $\Bbbk\langle x,y\rangle$-modules to finite-dimensional $H$-modules.

items.title: A remark on the reach and upper bounds on some extrinsic geometry invariants of submanifolds
items.summary: We consider a compact submanifold $M$ of a Riemannian manifold $N$ and we use the second variation formula as a tool to drive some geometric results on reach$(M, N)$ the reach of $M$ in $N$, including some useful relations between the extrinsic geometry of $M$ in $N$ and reach$(M, N)$. Our results generalize some theorems previously proved for the special case where $N$ is Euclidean space.

items.title: On identities in connected topological groups
items.summary: We construct a connected (indeed, path-connected) Hausdorff topological group G such that, for an odd n >= 665, the identity x^n = e holds in some neighbourhood of the identity but does not hold in the whole group. This answers in the negative a question of Mycielski and Aronszajn (Question 2.48 of the Kourovka Notebook). The construction uses the Graev extension of metrics to free topological groups and results of Adian and Adian-Atabekyan (for n > 10^10, alternatively, of Ol'shanskii and Ashmanov-Ol'shanskii) on free Burnside groups and their central extensions.

items.title: Symplectic Cuts and Moment Polyptychs of Hypertoric Varieties
items.summary: We study compact symplectic cuts of hypertoric varieties and characterise their smoothness. When the defining arrangement has a non-empty bounded base region, the fibre-rotation action has a proper moment map and gives compact Kähler orbifold cuts at regular levels. For a smooth hypertoric manifold, an outer-chamber cut, taken above the largest critical value of this moment map, is smooth if and only if the manifold is the cotangent bundle of its distinguished compact toric subvariety; that subvariety is then a product of projective spaces, and every positive level is regular with a smooth cut. If the compact core of a smooth hypertoric manifold is reducible, every outer-chamber cut has a boundary point with non-trivial cyclic isotropy and a singular coarse local quotient, whereas every cut below the smallest positive critical value is smooth. We introduce the moment polyptych, assembled from truncated arrangement regions, and recover the residual fixed points, tangent weights, and finite local groups from its edges and labelled lattice data. Restriction to arrangement flats is compatible with cutting and supplies the lower-dimensional models used in these calculations. The resulting local data are applied to equivariant quantisation in a companion paper.

items.title: Decay rates for monotone operator flows in the space of probability measures
items.summary: Motivated by the mean-field dynamics of large populations of interacting agents, we study the long-time behavior of flows driven by monotone demicontinuous operators on the Wasserstein space. For cocoercive operators, we prove that the flow converges to a zero of the operator and that the operator residual and the metric speed decay as $o(t^{-1/2})$, so that the population comes to rest (the agents asymptotically stop moving). We also consider Tikhonov regularized flows of merely monotone demicontinuous operators and show that the operator residual and the metric speed tend to zero, with rate $O(1/t)$ when the Tikhonov parameter is $α/t$ with $α\geq 1$, and that the trajectory converges to the zero of minimal second moment, which is a Dirac mass, so that the agents reach consensus (all agents reach the same point). Finally, we study a discrete analogue for nonexpansive operators and show that the generated sequence converges to the fixed point closest to a reference Dirac mass; this fixed point is again a Dirac mass, so that consensus is also reached under this scheme. The main arguments rely on a specially tailored superposition principle, which represents the flow as a curve in a fixed Hilbert space of random trajectories, where the crucial estimates are derived.

items.title: Explicit plane models for all Galois quotients of the Hermitian curve
items.summary: Let $H=k(x,y)$ be the Hermitian function field $y^q+y=x^{q+1}$ over $k=\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$, and let $G$ be a subgroup of its $k$-automorphism group $\operatorname{PGU}(3,q)$. We give a uniform construction of a plane model for $H^G$. For each of $x$ and $y$, we multiply its distinct translates under the stabilizer $S$ in $G$ of their common pole, then sum the translates of that product over $G/S$. The two resulting functions $U,V$ generate $H^G$. In $H^G$, their only pole is the restriction of the common pole, with coprime orders $a=q/|G_x|$ and $b=(q+1)/|G_y|$, where $G_x,G_y$ are the subgroups of $G$ fixing $x,y$, respectively. Their plane equation has degree $\max(a,b)\leq q+1$ and can be recovered from finitely many Laurent coefficients of $U,V$ at the common pole of $x,y$. All steps are effective given matrix generators of $G$. The total delta invariant of this affine model is $g(H^{G_xG_y})-g(H^G)=\frac{1}{2}(a-1)(b-1)-g(H^G)$. Consequently $g(H^G)\leq\frac{1}{2}(a-1)(b-1)$; when $g(H^G)\geq2$, the model is smooth if and only if $G=G_xG_y$. The generator construction also applies to other function fields admitting two functions whose only pole is a common rational place, with coprime orders.

items.title: Classifiyng metrically conical rational singularities
items.summary: We will in this article classify which rational complex surface singularities are metrically conical, that is have the bilipschitz type of their inner metric equivalent to that of a cone. This is done using the thick-thin decomposition for the inner geometry of a normal complex surface singularity and properties of rational singularities. The result is a family of singularities depending only on their topology which is given as a $3$-parameter family.

items.title: On Algebraic LNE models of complex affine algebraic curves
items.summary: We give a sufficient condition for an affine complex curve to have an algebraic complex LNE model.

items.title: Treewidth versus Hadwiger number: Graph classes with dominated balanced separators are quasi-linearly treewidth-Hadwiger bounded
items.summary: In a hereditary graph class $\mathcal{G}$, the treewidth of a graph in $\mathcal{G}$ is bounded by a function of the size of a largest clique minor of the graph if and only if the class $\mathcal{G}$ excludes some planar graph as an induced minor. Campbell et al. (arXiv 2024) conjectured that such a bounding function can always be chosen to be linear. We verify this conjecture for several classes of graphs (including even-hole-free graphs) and show that if a hereditary graph class $\mathcal{G}$ has dominated binary-weighted balanced separators, then the bounding function can be taken to be in ${O(h \log h)}$, where $h$ is the Hadwiger number. We say that $\mathcal{G}$ has dominated binary-weighted balanced separators if, for every ${G \in \mathcal{G}}$ and every $\mathsf{w} \colon V(G) \to \{0,1\}$, there is a set ${D \subseteq V(G)}$ of bounded size so that deleting the closed neighbourhood $N_G[D]$ of $D$ leaves each component with at most a fixed fraction of the total weight of $G$. Our result reduces the quasi-linear weakening of the conjecture of Campbell et al. to a conjecture of Gartland and Lokshtanov stating that every graph class excluding a planar graph as an induced minor admits dominated binary-weighted balanced separators.

items.title: Quasi-equatorial controlled switching in inertial magnetization dynamics
items.summary: We design exponentially decaying transverse magnetic fields for reliable and ultra-fast (picosecond) magnetization reversal governed by the inertial Landau--Lifshitz--Gilbert equation. The control construction uses an explicitly resolvable auxiliary model to select the field amplitude and characterize the influence of its decay rate, with the aim of obtaining reversal followed by relaxation without requiring a precisely timed interruption of the excitation. The auxiliary model is obtained through an equatorial approximation, and bounds on its latitude identify a regime consistent with quasi-equatorial motion. For the full nonlinear macrospin dynamics, an energy argument accounting for both inertial kinetic energy and the remaining field input provides a sufficient condition excluding backhopping, even while the exponential tail remains applied. Approximate confinement times and optimal decay rates are derived from the competition between field decay and inertial relaxation. Numerical simulations confirm the usefulness of these design estimates and identify their limitations near a capture boundary, where nearby pulses can lead to opposite final states. Spatially resolved inertial micromagnetic simulations further support reversal followed by relaxation over the simulated interval and quantify the transient departures from spatially coherent motion. The resulting approach combines explicit pulse design with a full-system energy certificate, while distinguishing rapid initial rotation from safe confinement and subsequent relaxation.

items.title: Vanishing Control Times for Single-Input Bilinear Quantum Systems under Rapid Drift Spectral Growth
items.summary: This paper investigates the asymptotic behavior, as the Hilbert space dimension tends to infinity, of the state-to-state control time of single-input bilinear quantum systems whose control operator is drawn from an isotropic (unitarily invariant) random ensemble. Relying on deterministic graph-theoretic bounds, namely star cuts of the interaction graph for the lower bound and spanning trees for the upper bound, and on integration over the Haar measure, we derive high-probability lower and upper bounds on the control time, expressed in terms of the empirical spectral variance and of the relative concentration of the drift spectrum. Whenever the spectrum grows fast enough (for instance polynomially with an exponent larger than 3/2, geometrically, or super-exponentially), the upper bound vanishes and the control time tends to zero in probability: in these cases, enlarging the Hilbert space constructively speeds up control.

items.title: A posteriori error estimates for higher-order BDF methods for parabolic partial differential equations
items.summary: We derive a posteriori error estimates for parabolic problems discretized by conforming finite elements in space and by the backward differentiation formula of order $k$ in time, with variable step-sizes for $k \le 3$ and constant step-size for $k = 4$. The key ingredient of the analysis is a polynomial $(k+1)$-point time reconstruction of degree $k$ of the approximate solution combined with the elliptic reconstruction. We conclude upper a posteriori error bounds in $L^\infty(L^2) \cap L^2(H^1)$ and in $L^\infty(H^1) \cap H^1(L^2)$. Numerical experiments for $k = 1, \dots, 4$ with linear and quadratic finite elements confirm the optimal orders of the estimators in time and in space.

items.title: Random Laguerre tessellations in hyperbolic space
items.summary: We introduce Laguerre tessellations in hyperbolic space as a weighted generalization of Voronoi tessellations and a hyperbolic analogue of Euclidean power diagrams. We present geometric and analytic constructions and establish conditions under which a collection of weighted points generates a well-defined tessellation. For Poisson point processes of weighted points, we derive necessary and sufficient conditions on the intensity measure ensuring that the resulting diagram is almost surely a tessellation. We then prove that hyperbolic Poisson-Laguerre tessellations are stable under intersections with totally geodesic subspaces, with an explicit transformation of the intensity measure. As applications, we identify the Poisson-Laguerre tessellations arising as sections of hyperbolic Poisson-Voronoi and ideal Poisson-Voronoi tessellations. In particular, the latter have unbounded cells, while their proper totally geodesic sections have bounded cells almost surely.

items.title: A Silverman-Meadows-type criterion for the null controllability of time-dependent coupled heat equations with non-diagonalizable diffusion matrices
items.summary: This paper is devoted to a uniform spectral Silverman-Meadows rank condition for the nullcontrollability of coupled systems of heat equations with time-dependent diffusion, coupling and control matrices. The proof relies on an adaptation of the Lebeau-Robbiano strategy combined with uniform finite-dimensional observability estimates associated with each Laplace eigenmode.

items.title: Gorenstein dimensions for stable Auslander algebras of Nakayama algebras
items.summary: Let $A$ be a Nakayama algebra and $\underline{\mathrm{Aus}}(A)$ its stable Auslander algebra. We introduce a new homological invariant, called the finitistic Gorenstein dimension, which coincides with the classical Gorenstein dimension whenever the latter is finite, and compute this invariant for $\underline{\mathrm{Aus}}(A)$ when $A$ has infinite global dimension. Combined with an accompanying criterion for the finiteness of the Gorenstein dimension of $\underline{\mathrm{Aus}}(A)$, our results provide a complete description of this dimension and verify the Gorenstein Symmetry Conjecture for this class of algebras. Furthermore, we show that the finitistic Gorenstein dimension of $ \underline{\mathrm{Aus}}(A) $ is also left-right symmetric, is explicitly related to the finitistic dimension of $A$, and can be attained among the injective dimensions of the projective $ \underline{\mathrm{Aus}}(A) $-modules corresponding to simple $A$-modules. Our proofs rely on computing injective dimensions in terms of distances in the coresolution forest of $A$, a combinatorial structure closely related to Ringel's coresolution quiver.

items.title: A resolution of the Erdős similarity problem in the large
items.summary: We show that for every unbounded set $A\subset\mathbb R$ and every $0<\varepsilon<1$, there exists a closed set $S\subset\mathbb R$ that has measure at least $1-\varepsilon$ in every unit interval and contains no nontrivial affine copy of $A$. This resolves the Erdős similarity problem in the large.

items.title: Symmetric compatibility of theta structures, with applications to change of level and isogenies
items.summary: Let $m,n,d >1$ be integers such that $n=md$ and let $(B, \mathscr{M}, Θ\_{\mathscr{M}})$ be a marked abelian variety of level $m$ over a field of odd characteristic. We study the theta structures of level $n$ for $\mathscr{M}^d$, and the theta structures on the abelian varieties $d$-isogenous to $B$, which are compatible with $Θ\_{\mathscr{M}}$. When $d$ is odd and coprime to $m$, they correspond to the isotropic subgroups of $B[n]$, and this correspondence underlies the known algorithms in theta coordinates. In general, this is no longer true. We introduce the notion of symmetric compatibility of a torsion point with a symmetric level subgroup, and we show that a subgroup of $B[n]$ isomorphic to $(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^g$ comes from a compatible theta structure if and only if it is isotropic and all its points are symmetric compatible. We extend to every $d$ Mumford's notion of compatible pairs of theta structures, defined by Mumford for $d=2$, and prove that it is equivalent to our notion, which can be tested on theta coordinates; we also describe exactly the remaining ambiguity, which explains the sign choices met when the duplication formula is used to change the level. As applications, we obtain change of level and isogeny algorithms without assuming that $d$ is odd and coprime to $m$, using $O(n^{3g} \log(d))$ and $O(n^{2g} \log(d))$ operations in the base field respectively. In particular, they give change of level algorithms for even $d$, and $2$-isogenies in level $4$ theta coordinates with an explicit control of the theta structure of the codomain.

items.title: Heights of Drinfeld modular polynomials and Hecke images
items.summary: We obtain explicit upper and lower bounds on the size of the coefficients of the Drinfeld modular polynomials $Φ_N$ for any monic $N\in\mathbb{F}_q[t]$. These polynomials vanish at pairs of $j$-invariants of Drinfeld $\mathbb{F}_q[t]$-modules of rank 2 linked by cyclic isogenies of degree $N$. The main term in both bounds is asymptotically optimal as $\mathrm{deg}(N)$ tends to infinity. We also obtain precise estimates on the Weil height and Taguchi height of Hecke images of Drinfeld modules of rank 2.

items.title: Energy Dissipation Along Trajectories and Wasserstein Gradient Flow of Aggregation-Diffusion Equations
items.summary: In this work, we established the Wasserstein gradient flow structure of nonlinear Fokker-Planck equations on bounded domains involving both nonlinear diffusion and nonlocal interaction effects. Our approach is based on stochastic analysis. More precisely, we investigated the associated stochastic differential equation (SDE) with normal reflection at the boundary from a trajectorial perspective and derived a semimartingale decomposition of the corresponding energy process. This decomposition leads to a trajectorial energy dissipation identity, which, together with the characterization of the metric derivative, allows us to establish the Wasserstein gradient flow structure of the aggregation-diffusion equation.

items.title: Predictive Neuromorphic Control of a Scanning Mirror System: An Event-Centric Framework
items.summary: Organizing control around events can reduce sensing and actuation demands while directly linking control decisions to the occurrence and timing of desired system behaviors. This paper proposes a novel event-centric model predictive control (MPC) framework that unifies event sensing, event prediction, and event regulation. Events define the feedback information, prediction horizon, and event-timing objectives, placing them at the center of predictive control design. The framework is developed for a scanning mirror system equipped with a baseline neuromorphic controller composed of spiking neurons that supports sparse actuation. The control objective is to achieve prescribed zero-crossing times and a desired scanning range while minimizing the mechanical energy transferred between the actuator and the mirror. A sampling-based algorithm is presented to obtain suboptimal solutions of the event-centric MPC optimization problem without requiring an explicit event-to-event prediction model. By grounding predictive optimization in events, the proposed framework opens a new direction for MPC design and its integration with neuromorphic control.

items.title: Triviality of metric fibrations over locally finite metric graphs
items.summary: In this note, we give a direct proof that every metric fibration over a geodesic metric space locally modeled on finite metric stars is isometrically isomorphic, over its base, to the $\ell^1$ product of its base and a fiber. Neither compactness nor completeness of the base is assumed. We also construct a nontrivial example over a closed interval with a truncated metric, showing that the local star condition alone does not imply the conclusion.

items.title: Sharp Proximity Bounds for Integer Programs with Few Rows
items.summary: We study the proximity between an optimal vertex of a standard form linear program with constraint matrix $A\in\mathbb{Z}^{m\times n}$ and an optimal integer solution. When $m = 2$, we prove the sharp infinity-norm bound $Δ-1$, where $Δ$ is the largest absolute maximal minor of $A$. When $m = 1$, we express the difference between an optimal LP vertex and an optimal integer solution as a nonnegative combination of certain generators in the kernel of $A$ with a bounded coefficient sum. This implies sharp proximity bounds for all norms when $m=1$. Combining this representation with its known counterpart for Hilbert bases due to Sissokho, we develop techniques that transfer results from $m=1$ to $m=2$. Along the way, for $m=2$, we prove that such a representation exists for an extended Gomory group relaxation and obtain the sharp infinity-norm bound $Δ$ for Graver basis elements. We also present a new short proof of Sissokho's result and lower bounds on the proximity for all $m$ and $Δ$.

items.title: The quantum double of the restricted quantum group $\mathbf{\overline{u}}_q(\mathfrak{sl_2})$
items.summary: In this paper, we construct the quantum double $D(\mathbf{\overline{u}}_q(\mathfrak{sl_2}))$ of the restricted quantum group $\mathbf{\overline{u}}_q(\mathfrak{sl_2})$. We describe the algebraic structure of $D(\mathbf{\overline{u}}_q(\mathfrak{sl_2}))$ by generators and relations. Moreover, we give the comultiplication $Δ$, the counit $\varepsilon$ and the antipode $S$, respectively. Finally, we classify all irreducible representations of $D(\mathbf{\overline{u}}_q(\mathfrak{sl_2}))$ when $p=2$.

items.title: Complete self-shrinkers with scalar curvature bounded below
items.summary: Let $X:M^n\to\mathbb R^{n+1}$ be a complete self-shrinker with constant squared norm of the second fundamental form. We prove that up to an orthogonal transformation, the image $X(M^n)$ is a sphere $S^n(\sqrt n)$, or a hyperplane $\mathbb R^n$ or a generalized cylinder $ S^k(\sqrt{k})\times\R^{n-k},\ 1\le k\le n-1$ if scalar curvature $R$ satisfies $R\geq -3/2$, which improves the recent results in \cite{CLW1}.

items.title: Mixed-integer dual network problems are solvable in strongly polynomial time
items.summary: In this paper we show that mixed-integer linear programming is solvable in strongly polynomial time if the constraint matrix is totally unimodular with at most two nonzero entries in every row. This is done by reducing the problem to an instance of minimization of an $L$-convex function.

items.title: On the Structure of Kähler-Ricci Shrinkers
items.summary: We prove that every complete Kähler--Ricci shrinker with nonnegative Ricci curvature is holomorphically isometric to $\mathbb{C}^k\times N^{n-k}$ for some $0\le k\le n$, where $\mathbb{C}^k$ is the Gaussian shrinker and $N$ is a compact Kähler--Ricci shrinker with nonnegative Ricci curvature. As a corollary, every complete Kähler--Ricci shrinker with quasi-positive Ricci curvature is compact. We also prove that every singular Kähler--Ricci shrinker on a Fano cone is a Ricci-flat Kähler cone.

items.title: Forecast Projection and Decision Regret: Theory and Evidence from Battery Arbitrage
items.summary: Decision-focused learning trains forecasts for the decisions they lead to, but forecasts are often projected onto known bounds before use. We study the resulting mismatch in battery arbitrage. When a battery starts and ends the day at the same charge level, a common shift in prices affects its schedule only through round-trip losses. As a result, decision-focused losses identify the forecast level only weakly. For the SPO+ and perturbed Fenchel-Young losses, we characterize the preferred level by a throughput-matching condition. Projecting forecasts onto a price cap can then remove profitable spreads and increase regret, even as prediction error falls. We give bounds on the change in regret, a dual-threshold condition under which a raw-optimal schedule remains optimal after clipping, and a general version of the mechanism for other problems with a conservation constraint. On 1,158 holdout days of the Indian day-ahead market, an equal-weight average of three statistical forecasts outperforms the five decision-focused variants tested. On 53 later days, with 62% of price blocks at the cap, no variant outperforms the regression or the equal-weight average, although most differences from the average are not significant. The results suggest that forecast post-processing should be treated as part of the predict-then-optimize pipeline.

items.title: From convolution pi-algebras to Rota-Baxter Hopf pi-algebras
items.summary: In this paper, we study Goncharov-type Rota-Baxter operators in the framework of group-graded Hopf pi-algebras. By constructing convolution pi-algebras as the core calculus tool, we systematically derive fundamental algebraic properties of Hopf pi-algebras, including antipode anti-homomorphism and generalized homomorphism compatibility. On this basis, we establish the axiomatic system of two classes of graded Rota-Baxter operators of weight 1 and weight -1, prove their bijective correspondence via the antipode, construct several non-trivial examples, and present two derived structures: descendant Hopf pi-algebras and image Hopf pi-subalgebras. This work enriches the operator theory of graded Hopf algebras and provides algebraic constructions for related research on graded Yang-Baxter equations.

items.title: Safe and Scalable Minimax Adaptive Control of Positive Systems
items.summary: This paper studies minimax adaptive control of positive linear systems with fixed unknown dynamics and nonnegative disturbances. We reformulate the problem by compressing the historical data into a vector and a positivity-induced consistency set containing the models compatible with the observations. Together with the physical state, these quantities form a sufficient information state and yield an exact reformulation as a standard minimax dynamic game. We allow the admissible input set to adapt to the current consistency set, ensuring positivity for every remaining feasible model. As inconsistent models are eliminated, the input set can expand, allowing less cautious control actions. For finite model sets, we derive an explicit solution to the Bellman inequality and construct a safe and stabilizing certainty-equivalence controller with robustness guarantees. The framework also accommodates structured classes of continuum model uncertainty whose consistency sets admit fixed, finite-dimensional representations, enabling scalable information-state updates.

items.title: Hamiltonian GKM spaces via Gromov-Witten theory
items.summary: We use equivariant Gromov-Witten theory to prove the generalised symplectic Mukai inequality for Hamiltonian GKM spaces with large pseudoindex or a special vertex, including smooth Schubert varieties. We also classify all Hamiltonian GKM graphs when the pseudoindex is at least the complex dimension, obtaining a Hamiltonian GKM analogue of the classical Kobayashi-Ochiai classification of complex projective space and complex quadrics. Of independent interest are our connectivity theorem for a low-magnitude subgraph of the GKM graph (reminiscent of Campana and Kollár-Miyaoka-Mori's rational chain connectedness of Fano manifolds), and a local Mukai-type theorem that applies at each vertex. We obtain corollaries on reflexive Delzant polytopes that are purely combinatorial in nature.

items.title: When do all iterates of $x^2 + a$ have maximal Galois group?
items.summary: We provide an (in our opinion) simpler proof of the main results of [Stoll1992,Li2020,Li2021] on the question for which integers $a$ the Galois groups of all iterates of $x^2 + a$ are maximal (equivalently, the associated arboreal Galois representation is surjective). At the same time, we extend the results to rational parameters $a$. The main result states that for a subset of rational numbers of relative density $1/2$ in the complement of a certain open interval, the maximality of the Galois group of the second iterate is sufficient for the arboreal Galois representation to be surjective. We also discuss experimental evidence suggesting that a similar statement involving the fourth iterate may hold in general. The results were obtained in collaboration with Claude (Anthropic's AI model); they are also formalized in Lean (except for the experimental evidence).

items.title: Improvement to characterizations of BMO in terms of endpoint bounds for commutators and some counterexamples
items.summary: In this paper, we extend the technique of Lerner, Ombrosi and Rivera-Ríos (Bull. Lond. Math. Soc. 51(1): 107--119, 2019) for the necessity of the strong-type boundedness of commutators to the endpoint case, and give characterizations of BMO via the endpoint bounds for commutators of singular integrals with rough kernels and related operators, which improve the conditions of Accomazzo (Israel J. Math. 228(2): 787--800, 2018), Guo et al. (J. Geom. Anal. 30(4): 3995-4035, 2020). We also give a characterization of BMO via the endpoint bounds for commutators of non-degenerate Calderón-Zygmund operators by removing the real-valued restriction on pointwise multiplier, which extend the results of Hytönen (J. Math. Pures Appl. (9) 156: 351--391, 2021) to the endpoint case. Finally, we find counterexamples to illustrate that weighted endpoint estimate of commutator of fractional integral operator does not necessarily imply $b\in{\rm BMO}$, and two-weighted endpoint estimate of Bloom type for commutator of Hilbert transform does not hold, which are missing for a long time.

items.title: A linear programming approach to finite copula interpolation
items.summary: We consider exact and interval-valued interpolation of multivariate copulas at arbitrary finite configurations in the unit cube. We first characterize when the prescribed data are compatible with a quasi-copula and derive explicit extremal quasi-copula envelopes. The copula interpolation problem is thereby reduced to a copula sandwich problem between these envelopes. Restricting them to the canonical rectangular grid generated by the data coordinates yields a finite linear feasibility system whose elementary-volume constraints are encoded by a cell--vertex incidence matrix. Farkas' lemma then identifies the criterion of Omladič and Stopar with an explicit certificate of infeasibility. Although this criterion is indexed by infinitely many formal cell combinations, we show that it suffices to test finitely many vertices of a sign-polytopal subdivision. We also extend the construction to $k$-increasing discrete quasi-copulas for $2\leq k\leq d$.

items.title: The Ordering Principle and Higher Dependent Choice
items.summary: We provide, for any regular uncountable cardinal $κ$, a new argument for Pincus' result on the consistency of $\mathrm{ZF}$ with the higher dependent choice principle $\mathrm{DC}_{<κ}$ and the ordering principle in the presence of a failure of the axiom of choice. We also generalise his methods and obtain these consistency results in a larger class of models.

items.title: Singular points of envelopes and offsets: a transition from 2D to 3D
items.summary: We recall properties of the offsets of a (plane) kiss curve and their singularities, then we make a transition to 3D, considering the surface obtained by revolution of the kiss curve about one of its axes. When pos?sible, geometric constructions using automated methods are performed. This induces a need to focus on algebraic computations. Networking be?tween different kinds of software is of utmost importance, in order to use their respective strengths (dynamic geometry, dragging points, strong al?gebraic computations, etc.). A core difference between the 2D and 3D situations is that automated commands existing in 2D are not available in 3D. This makes the DGS less relevant in 3D than in 2D. In 3D, most of the work must be performed with the CAS. The singular points of a kiss curve in the plane are tacnodes (cusps) and crunodes (self-intersection). The singularities are not isolated anymore and cuspidal edges appear. In this setting, implicitization is a heavy endeavour and we need another technology, related to AI; we describe this briefly. The 2D activities have been proposed to in-service teachers learning towards an advanced degree.

items.title: Frame Measure Rigidity and Fiber Entropy for Homogeneous Self-Similar Measures
items.summary: Let N >= 2, 0 < ρ< 1, and let b_0, ..., b_{N-1} be distinct vectors in \mathbb{R}^d. Let μbe the uniform homogeneous self-similar probability measure generated by the maps S_a(x) = ρx + b_a, without any separation assumption. We prove that if μadmits a frame measure, then the conditional coding measure is a Dirac mass for μ-almost every point. Equivalently, the coding map restricts to a Borel bijection between full-measure subsets of the symbolic space and the attractor. Consequently, the fiber entropy vanishes at every finite level, and μis exact dimensional with $\dim_H μ= \frac{\log N}{-\log ρ} \leq d.$ In particular, μadmits no frame measure whenever its Hausdorff dimension is strictly smaller than the similarity dimension. This excludes frame measures whenever Nρ^d > 1. As an application, we show that the uniform consecutive-digit Bernoulli convolution on the real line admits a frame measure in the range N^{-1} <= ρ< 1 if and only if ρ= N^{-1}.

items.title: Frege's election method: discrepancy, invariant polygons and Farey geometry
items.summary: We give a comprehensive study of Frege's modified election method as a proportional allocation rule and as a dynamical system. The method was introduced by Harrenstein, Lackner and Lackner (2022) as a modification of Frege's original proposal (1918), and it coincides with the greedy algorithm for the chairman assignment problem studied by Coppersmith et al. (2011). We consider several aspects of this method. First, we prove that the harmonic bound on the discrepancy earlier shown to be sharp for time-dependent vote proportions remains sharp for fixed vote proportions; we further quantify the restrictions on votes needed for the discrepancy to come close to this bound. Secondly, the method defines a dynamical system with a piecewise translation which, for almost every vote vector, has a unique compact attractor made up of finitely many polytopes, and every orbit is equidistributed on it, whatever choices are made at ties. Thirdly, for three parties, the dynamics is two-dimensional. We construct the invariant polygons explicitly and give a complete description of the geometry governing their bifurcations as the votes vary in the two-dimensional parameter space; this space is partitioned into a countably infinite number of ``Farey cells'' indexed by reduced fractions in $(0,\frac12]$, and each of them is further partitioned into a finite number of stability domains, separated by stability walls. In an open Farey cell indexed by a reduced fraction $u/v$, the invariant polygon has $4v+3$ vertices inside each stability domain and $4v+2$ on an internal stability wall. We construct the Farey cells explicitly and determine all stability walls and their endpoints; we also show that stability walls in different Farey cells combine to form a pattern of triangles.

items.title: Universal Approximation Theorem for Metaplectic Neural Operators
items.summary: We prove universal approximation for metaplectic neural operators on nonempty bounded Lipschitz domains. The nonlocal branches are whole-space metaplectic multipliers with zero extension and restriction, associated with any fixed free symplectic matrix. Assuming a smooth, globally Lipschitz, nonpolynomial activation, we obtain compact-uniform approximation of continuous operators from $C^s$ to $C^r$ and from $H^s$ to $H^r$ in the respective output norms, for arbitrary nonnegative integers $s,r$ and finite input and output channel dimensions. In the Sobolev setting, compact input sets must additionally be uniformly bounded in $L^\infty$. One hidden operator layer with one nonlocal branch suffices. A single scalar symbol atom and finitely many positional features are prescribed by the transform and domain independently of the target operator, compact set and accuracy. The proof combines averaging neural operator theory with an exact chirp-conjugated averaging identity and derivative estimates. The result includes Fourier and fixed nondegenerate fractional Fourier multiplier constructions.

items.title: High degree covers and genericity
items.summary: It is known that the genuine irreducible Iwahori-spherical representations of a tame $n$-fold Brylinski-Deligne cover of a $p$-adic split connected reductive group are all generic, when the degree $n$ is suitably large. This has been established by studying the the structure of the Gelfand-Graev representation as a module under the action of the Iwahori-Hecke algebra. In this paper, we present a different proof based on metaplectic Moy-Prasad theory.

items.title: Distributionally Robust Indirect-Feedback Stochastic MPC with Gelbrich Ambiguity Sets
items.summary: Stochastic model predictive control uses disturbance statistics to set safety margins. Errors in these statistics can invalidate the safety guarantees. This paper therefore describes the uncertainty in the disturbance mean and covariance by a prescribed Gelbrich ambiguity set. This contains distributions of any shape whose moments are close in the Gelbrich distance to the nominal values, including distributions with unbounded support. For linear time-invariant systems with additive disturbances, we build on the indirect feedback paradigm, propagate this moment uncertainty along the error dynamics, and obtain a closed-form constraint tightening that is computed offline. Robustness enters as a single additive term that grows with the size of the ambiguity set, so the online problem remains a quadratic program. Recursive feasibility and closed-loop satisfaction of conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) constraints hold for every disturbance distribution in the set. We illustrate the method on a linearized planar quadrotor.

items.title: Optimization-Based Path Planning for Industrial Manipulators: Experimental Validation in Additive Manufacturing
items.summary: Robotic additive manufacturing requires joint paths that reconcile robot feasibility with process-specific geometry. We develop an offline optimization-based path planner that combines joint-path regularity and self-collision penalties with process costs and constraints, so that a new process enters through its own reference, residuals, and tolerances. Full-path and boundary-coupled chunked optimization handle references of different lengths. Iterative Weight Tuning (IWT) determines the cost weights from the gaps between Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and their targets. In carbon-fiber winding and robotic 3D printing, the planned paths meet the geometric tolerances and all KPI targets, and both paths are executed on a UR10e, without extrusion for printing, with joint-level tracking recorded during execution.

items.title: The parental parsimony problem on binary, tree-child phylogenetic networks
items.summary: Phylogenetic reconstruction is one of the major challenges in computational biology. Among existing reconstruction methods for phylogenetic networks, an important subtask emerges in extending a leaf-labelling on a phylogenetic network to determine a most parsimonious tree inside the network. There exist different variants of this subtask depending on the biological model assumptions for which distinct evolutionary phenomena are captured by the network. In this article we assume that next to hybridization or recombination events, also allopolyploidy or incomplete lineage sorting are present. Then, finding the most parsimonious tree inside the network is called the parental parsimony score problem (PPS), a NP-hard combinatorial optimization problem. We provide the first constant-factor approximation for the PPS on arbitrary but fixed leaf labels and a class of networks on which the PPS remains NP-hard, namely binary, semi-simplex, tree-child phylogenetic networks. Furthermore, we introduce a novel exact solution algorithm for the PPS on binary, tree-child phylogenetic networks and analyze its performance on simulated data.

items.title: On $q$-Ary $t$-Designs from Codewords of Every Nonzero Weight in Linear Codes and Their Duals
items.summary: The paper investigates when the codewords of every nonzero weight in a linear code form a $q$-ary $t$-design and how to generalize the property to its dual code. We reduce the verification of this property to a prescribed range of low weights. Specifically, for MDS codes, we show that the $q$-ary $2$-design property at every nonzero weight is equivalent to that at any fixed nonzero weight. As an application, we prove that the codewords of every nonzero weight in a $[q+1,3,q-1]_q$ MDS code and its dual hold $q$-ary $2$-designs if and only if $q$ is even. We also establish a duality principle. When $t\le\min\{d,d^{\perp}\}$, the codewords of every nonzero weight in a linear code form a $q$-ary $t$-design if and only if the same property holds for its dual code. We then investigate narrow-sense antiprimitive BCH codes $\mathcal{C}_{(q,q+1,δ,1)}$ and their duals. For $q=2^m$ and $δ=2^r$ with $1\le r<m$ and $\gcd(r,m)=1$, the codewords of every nonzero weight in these codes form $q$-ary $2$-designs. Furthermore, for $δ=4$ and $q=2^{m}$ ($m\ge4$), we establish that the minimum-weight codewords of $\mathcal{C}_{(q,q+1,4,1)}$ form a $q$-ary $2$-design if and only if $m$ is odd.

items.title: Two-parameter versus one-parameter quantum groups: structural differences arising from the type~$D$ phenomenon
items.summary: This paper investigates several differences between two-parameter and one-parameter quantum (affine) algebras. We compare their Hopf algebra structures, algebra structures, automorphism groups of positive parts and extended Borel algebras, and module categories beyond the finite-dimensional setting. These differences are closely related to what we call \textit{``the type $D$ phenomenon''}, which widely appears in the structure of both finite and affine two-parameter quantum groups.

items.title: On the Spectral Estimation of VARMA Processes
items.summary: We consider the problem of estimating the power spectral density of a Vector-valued Autoregressive Moving-Average (VARMA) process. A well-established approach to accomplishing this task consists of formulating a moment problem that selects the spectral density maximizing an entropy-like index while matching certain moments of the underlying process. However, existing methods assume that the moving-average (MA) component is either fixed or scalar, thereby reducing the class of ARMA models over which the optimal spectral density is sought. In this paper, we propose a new moment problem, based on the notion of transportation entropy, for learning the spectral density of a VARMA process without fixing the MA component or restricting it to be scalar.

items.title: Resolution of Vinzant's Conjecture on Phase Retrieval Injectivity
items.summary: Let $A\in\mathbb C^{N\times M}$ with $N=4M-5$ has independent standard complex Gaussian entries. We prove that the probability that the phase retrieval map generated by $A$ is injective is strictly smaller than $1$, and is $O(M^{-1})$ as $M\to \infty$. This proves a conjecture of Cynthia Vinzant, which was later restated by Afonso S. Bandeira in \cite{bandeira2026randomstrasse101}. The main result of this paper was obtained using generative AI, in particular GPT6-Astra, GPT 5.6-sol, and the Rethlas system.

items.title: Delay-Certified Readiness Barriers for Overactuated Multirotor Allocation Without Lipschitz Constants
items.summary: Overactuated multirotors can produce the same wrench with many rotor-speed combinations, some of which leave the vehicle unable to change its wrench quickly, e.g., to reject a gust. Readiness barriers keep this ability, the readiness, above a floor, but only in continuous time; with sampled commands and varying speed-controller delays, the available robustness bound covers less than one millisecond. We remove this limit by exploiting the structure of the problem: each rotor responds monotonically and in closed form to its own torque, so the speeds reachable under uncertain switching times lie in a cheaply computed box, and the lowest readiness over that box sits at a corner known in advance. This yields a Lipschitz-free test that a command keeps the readiness above its floor until the next sample, plus a fallback torque that keeps the vehicle on a certified plan. In hexarotor simulations with 2--40~ms delays and $\pm2$~ms jitter, the filter never violated the floor. At $10\pm2$~ms, it matched a delay-compensating predictor within the design envelope and cost 2--30\% more tracking error beyond it, where the predictor alone violated the floor in 2 to 16 of 16 missions. A tuned robust predictor was also safe with synchronous switching, but not with per-rotor jitter.

items.title: On the minimum number of entries in a set of maximal mutually orthogonal partial Latin squares
items.summary: In superimposed form, a set of $k\ge2$ mutually orthogonal partial Latin squares of order $n$ is said to be maximal if no additional $k$-tuple may be inserted into any empty cell without violating orthogonality or the Latin property. For $k=2$ and $n\ge 21$ it is shown that the minimum number of filled cells in such a square is $\lceil n^2/3 \rceil$. Likewise for $k=3$ and $n\ge 44$ the minimum number of filled cells is $\lceil n^2/4 \rceil$ or $\lceil n^2/4 \rceil+1$, depending on the residue of $n$ modulo 4. In each case it is shown that the extremal systems are essentially those produced by a construction presented in the paper. A similar result is obtained for all $k\ge4$ for minimal systems that have a certain balance property, and it is conjectured that for sufficiently large $n$, even without this balance property, the extremal systems always correspond to those produced by this construction.

items.title: Adaptive stabilization of a leaderless bearing-constrained formation with disturbances
items.summary: In this paper, we consider the problem of regulating and maintaining a target formation characterized by a set of bidirectional bearing constraints under disturbances. The agents in the formation are modeled by single integrators with deterministic bounded continuous disturbances of which both actual function and upper bound are unavailable for the control design. Due to the time-varying disturbances, the target formation is time-varying. We propose displacement/bearing-only based adaptive sliding mode control laws to uniformly asymptotically stabilize the time-varying target formation and reject the matched disturbances, and provide sufficient conditions to prevent possible collisions. A time-dependent adaptive design method is provided to convert the displacement-based control law to a bearing-only one. In addition, to alleviate chattering phenomena from sliding mode control, smooth adaptive control laws are introduced to guarantee uniform global boundedness of the desired formation. Finally, simulation results are given to support the analysis.

items.title: Triangle Factors in the Semi-Random Graph Process
items.summary: The semi-random graph process is a single player game which starts with an empty graph on $n$ vertices and in each round the player is offered a random vertex and connects it to a vertex selected according to some strategy $\mathcal{S}$. The goal is, in as few rounds as possible, to arrive at a graph that satisfies some graph property $\mathcal{P}$. The main contribution of this work is to show that there is a strategy $\mathcal{S}$ which creates a $K_3$-factor in at most $2.929329 \, n$ rounds w.h.p.

items.title: The Landau equation in a domain
items.summary: This work deals with the Landau equation in a bounded domain with the Maxwell reflection condition on the boundary for any (possibly smoothly position dependent) accommodation coefficient and for the full range of interaction potentials, including the Coulomb case. We establish the global existence and a constructive asymptotic decay of solutions in a close-to-equilibrium regime. This is the first existence result for a Maxwell reflection condition on the boundary and that generalizes the similar results established for the Landau equation for other geometries in \cite{GuoLandau1,GS1,GS2,MR3625186,MR4076068}. We also answer to Villani's program \cite{MR2116276,MR2407976} about constructive accurate rate of convergence to the equilibrium {(quantitative H-Theorem)} for solutions to collisional kinetic equations satisfying a priori uniform bounds. The proofs rely on the study of a suitably linear problem for which we prove that the associated operator is hypocoercive, the associated semigroup is ultracontractive, and finally that it is asymptotically stable in many weighted $L^\infty$ spaces.

items.title: Rank Reversals in Efficient Vectors for Pairwise Comparisons
items.summary: Studied are the orders among alternatives given by efficient vectors for a reciprocal matrix A. The focus is upon: 1) existence of efficient vectors with a given order and 2) discrepancies between the ranking for a pair of alternatives resulting from an efficient vector and from the corresponding entry of A, called rank reversals. We use matrix intervals in which the consistent matrices built from efficient vectors lie. The existence of efficient vectors (or those from constituent convex subsets) with a rank reversal at a given position is characterized. The minimum number of rank reversals for a reciprocal matrix among all weight vectors is described and it is shown that there is an efficient vector that has this number of rank reversals. A way to construct such a vector is given. The order transitive and the uniformly ordered reciprocal matrices are shown to be, respectively, the matrices for which there is an efficient vector with no rank reversals and the matrices for which all efficient vectors have no rank reversals. The effects on rank reversals of addition and deletion of alternatives are also discussed. Using numerical experiments, the frequencies of rank reversals in certain formulaic weight vectors are given.

items.title: Topological triviality of exact Lagrangian Cobordisms
items.summary: Inspired by the rigidity of exact Lagrangian submanifolds, a conjecture by P.~Biran and O.~Cornea asks if a simple exact Lagrangian cobordism $W$ in a tame exact symplectic manifold is always ``symplectically trivial'' (i.e. the Lagrangian suspension of an Hamiltonian isotopy). In this short note, we prove a topological version of this conjecture~: if the cobordism has dimension at least $6$, it is always topologically trivial. This extends a previous work of Lara Suarez who reduced the question to proving an injectivity result among fundamental groups.

items.title: Automorphisms of the Reduced Finitary Power Monoid of $\N^d$
items.summary: Given an additive semigroup $S$, the collection of its nonempty finite subsets can be equipped with the setwise addition \[ X + Y = \{x + y : x \in X, \; y \in Y\}, \] forming a semigroup denoted by $\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{fin}}(S)$, which is called the finitary power semigroup of $S$. If $S$ is a monoid with identity $0$, the finite nonempty subsets containing $0$ form a submonoid $\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{fin},0}(S)$, known as the reduced finitary power monoid, whose identity element is the singleton $\{0\}$. Let $d$ be a positive integer, $\mathbb{N}$ the set of nonnegative integers, and $\mathbb{N}^d = \{(a_1, a_2, \dots, a_d) \mid a_i \in \mathbb{N}\}$. For the one-dimensional case \(d=1\), Tringali and Yan (\textit{J. Comb. Theory, Ser. A}, \textbf{209} (2025)) established that the only nontrivial automorphism of $\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{fin},0}(\mathbb{N})$ is the involution $X \mapsto \max X - X$. In this paper, we focus on the higher-dimensional case $d \ge 2$. We prove that $\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{fin},0}(\mathbb{N}^d)) \cong S_d$, meaning that every automorphism is inner, induced by a permutation of the coordinate directions. This reveals a sharp contrast with the one-dimensional setting, where non-inner symmetries exist.

items.title: A Dynamic Survey of Soft Set Theory and Its Extensions
items.summary: Soft set theory provides a systematic framework for parameterized decision-making by associating each parameter with a subset of a given universe, thereby enabling structured representations of uncertainty [1, 2]. Over the past decades, the theory has evolved into a broad range of extensions, including hypersoft sets, superhypersoft sets, TreeSoft sets, bipolar soft sets, and dynamic soft sets, while also establishing connections with various mathematical disciplines, particularly topology and matroid theory. This book presents a comprehensive survey of soft set theory and its principal extensions, with particular emphasis on parameter spaces, value spaces, representative mathematical constructions, and the underlying assumptions necessary for rigorous comparisons among different frameworks. It carefully distinguishes established definitions from the literature from exploratory formulations and critically examines the limitations of selected claims concerning representation and reduction. Building upon the first edition, this second edition introduces additional concepts and illustrative examples, addresses previously identified mathematical inconsistencies and typographical errors, and refines the overall structure and presentation to enhance mathematical rigor, clarity, and readability.

items.title: Geometry-Dependent Approximation and Stability Properties of Shallow ReLU$^k$ Networks on Bounded Euclidean Domains
items.summary: On bounded Euclidean domains, we study how hidden-parameter geometry affects shallow ReLU$^k$ networks through results on approximation rates, saturation-type lower bounds, Gram and stiffness matrix spectra, Bernstein and Marcinkiewicz--Zygmund inequalities, discrete least-squares recovery, and inverse approximation. Our analysis uses smooth localization and dyadic Fourier estimates. We quantify parameter geometry by the fill distance $h$ and antipodal separation distance $\underline h$. For the prescribed network space $L_n^k$, representative approximation estimates take the form \begin{equation*} \begin{aligned} \inf_{g_n\in L_n^k}\|f-g_n\|_{\mathcal L^2(Ω')}&\lesssim h^r\|f\|_{\mathcal H^r(Ω)},\\ \inf_{g_n\in L_n^k}\|f-g_n\|_{\mathcal L^2(Ω)}&\gtrsim \underline h^{\frac{d+2k+1}{2}}\|f\|_{\mathcal L^2(Ω')}. \end{aligned} \end{equation*} The upper bound exploits target regularity up to the critical order $\frac{d+2k+1}{2}$, while the lower bound applies asymptotically to fixed targets smoother than this order. The upper estimate holds on an interior subdomain $Ω'$, whereas the lower estimate concerns the larger domain $Ω$. We also obtain geometry-dependent spectral estimates that quantify conditioning and coefficient stability.
